utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Will the Court Officer please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-95-5/18-T, the Prosecutor versus Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Today we are continuing the trial proceedings with the Defence opening statement, which has been scheduled for the full morning today and continuing tomorrow morning. Before we proceed, I would like to have the appearances. For the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. Alan Tieger, Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff, and Iain Reid appear for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Mr. Karadzic, would you introduce the members of your team present in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Excellencies. With me are my legal advisors, Mr. Peter Robinson, and Mr. Marko Sladojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I also note that Mr. Richard Harvey is present here upon the instruction of the Trial Chamber. His role in the trial is yet to be determined and we will do so after Mr. Karadzic's opening statement and when the hearing of evidence begins. Mr. Harvey, I wonder if you could introduce the other members of your team who accompany you today.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President and Your Honours. I'm accompanied by Ms. Mirjana Vukajlovic today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before I give the floor to Mr. Karadzic for his opening statement, I would like to note that this opening statement is being given pursuant to Rule 84 of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence rather than Rule 84 bis. Mr. Karadzic, you will have the opportunity at a later stage, should you so choose, to make a Rule 84 bis statement, in which case the provisions of that Rule shall apply and the Chamber can decide what probative value, if any, to ascribe to your statement. There is one further matter to raise for purpose of the planning of the -- today's or tomorrow's hearing. The Trial Chamber denied the accused's motion for the further postponement of the trial last Friday, 26th of February. In that decision, the Trial Chamber set the dead-line for the accused to make a request for certification to appeal the decision, if he so wishes, by today, and I was told just now that the accused filed a request for certification to appeal the decision. Can I get the confirmation? I see nodding. We need some voice for the purpose of transcript. Is it Mr. Robinson or Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. If I can take the indulgence of Mr. Karadzic to answer your question, I would say that yes, we have filed that this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I welcome you again. In that case, Mr. Tieger, I wonder whether we -- the Chamber can have your response by the end of today or you wish to respond orally first thing tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's -- that's fine, Your Honour. I can probably respond first thing tomorrow morning or shortly before the conclusion of these proceedings. It should be no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Then I now give the floor to you, Mr. Karadzic, for your opening statement. Please bear in mind that we will need to break at approximately 10.20 for 20 minutes' break for the first break, and at 12.00 noon for half an hour for the second break. This regime will apply in the future hearings that will take place in the morning session. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just briefly, I wanted to mention the Prosecution's motion of February 23rd regarding a cautionary measure, and I don't know if the Trial Chamber's remarks to date reflect its conclusions in that regard or if that was -- if that slipped off the agenda, but I wanted to point out that the Prosecution does have that motion pending, and would hope that could be addressed before the accused commenced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger, for your reminder. I dealt with only part of it, and the remainder will be dealt with after the opening statement. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would first like to greet all the active and passive participants of this session. I stand here before you not to defend the mere mortal that I am but to defend the greatness of a small nation in Bosnia-Herzegovina which, for 500 years, has had to suffer and has demonstrated a great deal of modesty and perseverance to survive in freedom. I don't want to defend myself by saying that I wasn't important or that I didn't occupy an important post while I was serving my people, nor will I shift the blame to someone else. I will defend that nation of ours and their cause, which is just and holy, and in that way I shall be able to defend myself, too, and my nation, because we have a good case. We have good evidence and proof, and if I'm given sufficient time and resources to prepare my Defence, I shall be able to do so and it will be to our advantage. Therefore, the only thing that I expect here is to be given the opportunity to have a well-prepared defence and to present my case here in a proper manner, to show you the substance and crux of this matter and everything that hasn't been uncovered yet and hasn't been realised. I will start by describing a situation in my country. At the elections in 1990, and they were the first democratic elections at which many dissidents appeared because before that it wasn't a multi-party system. In the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, we had seven members, two Serbs, two Croats, two Muslims, and a representative for the minorities. My Serbian Democratic Party was in this seventh place, and the nomination there was the president of the Jewish community in Bosnia-Herzegovina, who was not a member of the SDS, but we did however consider that he represents, in the best sense of the word, the rest, the others. And apart from that, the community is very significant in Sarajevo because after the persecution in Spain, the Jews came to Sarajevo and have significant traces there and have contributed to Sarajevo's development. The Party of Democratic Action has put lamb's clothing on a wolf, a wolf in lamb's clothing on Mr. Ganic, called him a Yugoslav for this opportunity, and of course he was elected to this post which belonged to the minorities or the others. And that is the well-known gentleman who became famous when he slaughtered innocent soldiers who were withdrawing from -- in Sarajevo in Dobrovoljacka Street, and the well-known order he gave over the radio, As soon as Alija gets out of his car, kill them all. So that is how the SDA and the Muslim community in Bosnia -- in Bosnia-Herzegovina achieved supremacy in a body where parity was supposed to prevail. The Serbs had an even better candidate which they could have once again put in lamb's clothing, and somebody who declared himself as a Yugoslav, but we consider that that wasn't done in proper society because it wasn't democracy and it wasn't an honest and sound basis for life together and progress in general. And it was almost an innocent child's game in comparison to what the state organs, the joint state organs, did for the war policy of the Party of Democratic Action that was geared towards gaining as much advantage to their own community and inflicting detriment on the Christian majority, that is to say, the Serbs and the Croats. Now, why did the leaders of the Party of Democratic Action do this in the first place? Not only because it was the basic model of the fundamentalist way of thinking and acting, that is to say, domination, supremacy, privileges, 100 per cent power, just as it was in the days of the Ottoman Empire, but first and foremost, to gain one more vote in the Presidency in order to achieve the Islamist goal, that is to say, a state of the kind that the players in our drama had envisaged 50 years earlier. There were some very subtle games afoot in cadre terms and so on, but that was nothing compared to this, because the goals of the Communists were not such. They were ideological ones. However, these were fundamental goals changing the destiny and appearance of a whole region and the destiny of several nations and ethnic groups within it. Therefore, secession of Bosnia-Herzegovina in this case was the goal, and not only secession which could not be carried out in a legal way, but the establishment of a system and a regime and a state structure which I'm going to depict to you here and present my arguments to show you what it was like. And on the basis of the proof and evidence you will be able to see what they envisaged, and what was planned to result. So this -- there was this need to have one more vote, one extra vote, but not only that was enough, because the substance of the requirements of the SDA was to have Bosnia 100 per cent for them, and that was the basic way in which they were thinking. Bosnia is ours. The Serbs are guests here, and God knows the Croats, too, when they didn't need them to leave Yugoslavia anymore, and so they have to obey. That is how the Christian majority is treated to this day. And what would that treatment become if they managed to increase their birth rate by political means? Nobody minds the natural increase in the population, but if by political means, by immigration, forced resettlement of Muslims from Sandzak, the talked-about immigration of 4 million Turks who allegedly have roots in Bosnia – you can imagine yourselves what that would look like, and they wrote about this in their papers. When the United States, in 1995, decided to end the war which they had been waging in Bosnia-Herzegovina, their ambassadors, Holbrooke and Bildt, write and say that Holbrooke told the Islamic leadership, they said, What do you want us to negotiate for you? Do you want to have 100 per cent power in 30 per cent of Bosnia, or 30 per cent of power in 100 per cent Bosnia? You cannot have 100 per cent power in 100 per cent Bosnia. And that is the crux of all our crisis and the war and the crisis that is still ongoing today, and you can clearly see that the State Department and Ambassador Holbrooke understood this. But precisely that thing that they cannot get, that even their most powerful ally would not grant them, the same thing that they wanted in 1914 and in 1941, - they want it still; now, of course, they want it in a different constellation of players. The Islamic fundamentalists pursued it in 1991-1995, and they’ll continue to want that until the borders have been precisely defined or jurisdictions of these entities. For as long as people in Bosnia or a group in Bosnia has the chance of seizing a hundred per cent of Bosnia, a hundred per cent of power in a hundred per cent of Bosnia, you will not have peace in Bosnia. Now let's make this quite clear. I'm not speaking about all the Muslims, nor am I speaking about the whole of the Party of Democratic Action. What I’m referring to is a core that is plotting and conniving and which was responsible for all this. I'm not making a plea for the fact that Muslims should be Serbs, but we consider them – many consider them – as Serbs. All their great minds, from Mehmet-Pasa Sokolovic, Osman Dzikic, Hasan Rebcic [phoen], (Rebac) Mesa Selimovic, to the great minds of our day, were and remain Serbs. In the Serbian culture, which is theirs as much as it is mine, they achieved greatness. But that is not the point of this discussion. Simply, let everyone be what they want to be. Not even a whole of the SDA party is responsible for what was happening and what is happening. Within the SDA there is a conspiracy core which has been identified by the leaders of the Muslim Bosniak organisation, other Muslim parties, Mr. Zulfikarpasic and Professor Filipovic have identified them, and they left the SDA when they saw what was afoot and what was going on. And a Muslim intellectual, before the elections, wrote Izetbegovic a letter, when he left the SDA, he said, "Do you think that the Serbs are fools that and they don't see what you're doing?" Therefore, that was the reason for him distancing himself from the party, because he was a man of vision and saw what was going to happen ultimately. Now what was this conspiracy core within the SDA? They were the young Muslims. And it is these young Muslims that were formed as an affiliation or a reflection of the Muslim brothers in Egypt, for example, who, as you know, killed Sadat and did goodness knows what else. Now the Prosecution can say that's tu quoque, that's not important, they're not being tried. But why aren't they being tried? Why were the direct perpetrators of heinous crimes on their side, men with blood on their hands up to their elbows, acquitted here? Probably because the indictments weren't what they were supposed to be and it wasn't -- it was easy to have them liberated, acquitted. This is not about tu quoque; it’s a fact that cannot be bypassed. Their conduct gave rise to our conduct, they conditioned our conduct 100 per cent. I am surprised and concerned as well to see how the Prosecution is acting in various situations. They would like to have a trial without any corpus delecti. They would like us to say, All right, let's just get together and agree to prosecute and find people guilty. But this Defence has much criticism to make of that stance and will not allow it to go forward, to proceed in that way because it would appear -- and it would appear that the Prosecution has struck an agreement with our enemies in war, or as we like to say, without joking, that the Prosecutor is trying to turn this Tribunal into a disciplinary commission of NATO. And to say that this is not an exaggeration, you will hear from the high-ranking officers of this Tribunal itself to the effect that everybody who -- that NATO planned to liquidate Karadzic, and everybody who went against the grain of NATO had to be taken to trial.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "I want to speak you -- I want to speak with you about Karadzic. SFOR, in particular the United States, they will try to locate Karadzic. Karadzic knows, he knows perfectly that he is in danger because if they locate him, he will not be transferred to The Hague alive. It will be an operation and after shot down Karadzic, they'd say, 'Yes, he was armed, and it was reacting.' [Indiscernible] and why I'm saying that, because I am investigating about the agreement between Karadzic and Holbrooke. I am investigating and I am getting some good -- some good evidence that it's true. But if it is true, as it seems in my -- in my investigation, it is more element to fear that they will kill Karadzic. "The substance is that surrender is better than murder. "Yes, yes. There's no parliament anymore, no government anymore. It's no more federation. It's just Bosnia-Herzegovina. It's not existing anymore Republika Srpska. It's finished. It's finished Republika Srpska. Now it's only Bosnia."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems to me that I even had friends in the OTP, because this is a better version than having me liquidated, isn't it? However, I believe that today this can only make us realise what was going on. The OTP is trying to link up this accused person and the chaos and tragedy of civil war, and may I remind you that not a single war in our part of the world did not also become a civil war. The aggressor always managed to turn people against each other, and that's the way it's been since time immemorial but particularly in modern times, in the 19th and 20th century. So the OTP is trying to link up this accused person with the chaotic, tragic developments of a civil war that could be expected and that were even envisaged. They're trying to accuse me of planning, aiding, abetting, instigating, and whatever else you have, the removal of Muslims and Croats from the territories in Bosnia-Herzegovina that Serbs lay a claim to. They are claiming their own territories, as you will see, and that is not a crime, and I don't think that the OTP treats it as such. The Prosecution is behaving as if this were a crime. We're going to hear that often enough here, and that just shows how false this entire situation is, what a fabrication all of this is. The Prosecution crosses this bridge, as it were, very quickly, and they're saying that laying claim to one's own territory and establishing a political party, and taking part in elections, and political defence from political attacks, and armed defence from armed attacks, and self-defence and self-organisation in a condition when a state organism falls apart, and everything that was the Serb democratic response to attacks from either side, and everything that Serbs did as part of their own legitimate defence, all of that is being treated as a crime, and they quickly move on to chaotic developments which happen in civil wars. After all, everyone knew that that would happen. That is what was envisaged. And people knew that’s what was going to happen. Now, this fine bridge between the accused and everything that happened is something that the Defence considers to be very important. We want to go back to that bridge because there is that intention that is referred, to remove non-Serbs from territories that Serbs in Bosnia claimed. The Defence doesn't want to deal with this in minute detail as to who killed who, how the first, the second, the third, or fourth party behaved, because we will see during these proceedings that there were four parties at war in this situation. The Prosecution has to prove this basic thesis of theirs. Without proving that they cannot prove joint criminal enterprise or any responsibility on the part of Republika Srpska and its government, its organs, its police, army, et cetera. A few things to begin with. First of all, Republika Srpska was not the political objective of the Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Their objective was Yugoslavia. Secondly, Republika Srpska was created out of necessity and as a very painful compromise of the Serbs in order to agree to leave Yugoslavia. I am going to enumerate Serb priorities. The first was the preservation of Yugoslavia as big as possible, if possible consisting of all of its six republics, and that was the superior prime objective. If the Muslims and Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina do not wish to remain in Yugoslavia, the Serb objective -- the secondary Serb objective was that they remain in Yugoslavia, just like West Virginia remained with the north, with the American Federation, whereas the majority of Virginia did join the Confederacy. Western Virginia exists to this day because Lincoln, a great president, agreed to that and recognised it. So we haven't got an East Virginia, there's only a West Virginia; right? Now are we to regret that these are not times of great presidents, so that we could not see a proper solution to the Serb issue and to the situation in the Balkans in general. In the same way, Northern Ireland continues to exist. Most of Ireland gained independence. However, part of Ireland did not. It remained within the United Kingdom. This variant with Northern Ireland, that is to say, Serbs with the Serb territories, genuine Serb territories, as you will see, the Serbs of Bosnia-Herzegovina are the oldest population there because most of the population were Serbs in the first place. So anyway, this was Mr. Izetbegovic's idea. He even signed on to that idea in his agreement, with the related declaration, with Mr. Krajisnik in September 1993. Serb -- the third Serb priority was the independence of a Serb constituent unit of the state in Bosnia-Herzegovina which Mr. Izetbegovic did not challenge either. The fourth, very painful option was that all of Bosnia leaves Yugoslavia on the condition that the Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina have their constituent unit of their own in some kind of a confederation of an alliance of Bosnian states. That variant, but less favourable in terms of integration in Bosnia-Herzegovina, was offered to us by the European Community within Lord Carrington's conference. Ambassador Cutileiro was in charge of Bosnia within the scope of that conference. That is the well-known Cutileiro Plan. Rest assured that this was the list of Serb priorities. Every one of these variants ensured the preservation of peace and the achievement of Croat and Muslim optimal objectives through Serb lenience. These were minimum objectives as far as the Serbs were concerned, far from maximum. What joint criminal enterprise can stand in the face of this fact? What I'm going to present here is marble truth, and this is one of the truths that I am referring to. How can there be a joint criminal enterprise? What is it that Serbs could do if all Serb compromises had been agreed to? Thirdly, the Prosecution constructs this alleged intention of ours to expel Muslim and Croats from their own home on this false presumption that we consider Republika Srpska to be our home at the time. At that time, the home of the Serbs was Yugoslavia, not Bosnia-Herzegovina, let alone Republika Srpska that hadn't even been created yet. We are going to prove that there never was any intention, any idea, let alone plan, to expel Muslims and Croats from Republika Srpska. This is what another Chamber of this Tribunal says in the first instance judgement to -- of Mr. Krajisnik. It has to do with the words of Radovan Karadzic on the 14th of February, 1992, just before the war, and the Trial Chamber concludes that Karadzic, at a party meeting, a closed Plenary meeting of the party, said that they will be careful to govern responsibly at the local level and make sure there is no fleeing en masse. Because, at that moment, the conference was already at some advanced stage; agreements had been reached, although not yet signed; but an agreement had been reached with Holbrooke that there would be three Bosnias. So that is the most painful variant for the Serbs, that there will be three Bosnias. That had already been achieved, and Karadzic says, before 200 people that are responsible for life on the ground, as it were, to be careful, that there would be no fleeing from our areas, quote/unquote. This Trial Chamber admits that and says that Karadzic, even on the 14th of February, 1992, bore in mind the interest of others. Therefore, everything prior to 14 February 1992 must be dropped. Until then there was no joint criminal enterprise. We have to identify now what is the moment of birth of this joint criminal enterprise that is called the expulsion of Croats and Muslims from Republika Srpska. That is part of the words of caution of Radovan Karadzic to the people in charge of affairs. Now, the next reference. We have to realise that on the 14th of February, 1992, there was no joint criminal enterprise. That was not its moment of birth. It was not born on 18 March because that was when the Lisbon Agreement was reached. The Agreement was reached and it was the solution. Now we go to the 27th of March, and Karadzic is speaking at the Assembly of the Serbian people, and you see: "A war in Bosnia and Herzegovina will not solve anything. We must study the situation regarding the saving of lives, property and territory. We have no other plans." That is Karadzic's response to a question put by one of the assemblymen. The only plan of the Serbs at the time was to protect people, property, and territory, and wait for a political solution. Then we have to move that time forward, to move forward the moment of birth of the joint criminal enterprise. On the 12th of April, when the war had already broken out, with Ambassador Cutileiro we signed a cease-fire, all three parties. On the 12th of March we signed a cease-fire, and on the evening of the 12th of March, the Muslim side, the SDA, sent -- Hasan Efendic sent this well-known order, instruction to launch an all-out attack against the JNA and Serbs throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina. So on the Serb side, even on the 12th of April there is no joint criminal enterprise. On the 22nd of April, Karadzic presents a plan for the cessation of hostilities and bringing the crisis to an end. I have to note that on the 12th of April, within that cease-fire, what was concluded was to work even faster on the maps involved in the Cutileiro Plan. So on the 22nd of April, there is no joint criminal enterprise either. Then you're going to see August, for instance. Karadzic is fighting for having Muslims and Croats elected to positions in the judiciary and in government. Up until then, members of the Presidency could make appointments, and I appointed 18 Muslims and Croats to positions in the judiciary, in courts of law. Afterwards these powers were returned to the Assembly. It says here, as we said yesterday, we should see whether it is the right person involved rather than that person's ethnic background. And Karadzic says, As for others, you have to be aware of the fact that they will always have proportionate participation in the government. The war had already started. There was a lot of bloodshed. There were a lot of clashes, conflicts. There is some restraint and there are some reservations in terms of appointing Croats and Muslims. However, Karadzic and Popovic and others who asked for the Judges to be appointed quickly asked that ethnic background not being taken into account, only the personal eligibility of all candidates and that there should be proportionate representation of all the ethnic communities there. I have to remind you what this looked like on the 18th of March. You will see that all of 1991 was burdened with inter-ethnic tensions and the Serbs gave way, whenever possible, just in order to ensure peace in Bosnia-Herzegovina. On the 18th of March, we agreed that there would be three Bosnia-Herzegovinas within one Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is to say, to carry out a Switzerlandisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that it will be outside Yugoslavia. That is the most painful compromise that the Serbs had to make. At that point in time, we all three parties accepted this and expressed our great pleasure. All three parties then concluded that they all had maps, although the SDA claimed that they did not have maps, and we came to the conclusion that 80 per cent were not controversial. Serbs agreed to 80 per cent of the maps, and the Muslims and the Croats agreed up to 80 per cent as to what the others would have, et cetera. The Muslim fared the best, and this is what this gentleman, Mr. Irfan Ajanovic is saying. He said that 82 per cent of the population will live in their own ethnic unit and that the Serb people make up 50 per cent of the population, the Serb unit, and no one ever mentions any population exchanges or any kind of population movement, except for voluntary migrations, if people simply want to move. Mr. Izetbegovic, while working with me and very good relations -- well, we enjoyed very good relations during our work on the maps, and I repeated that at that meeting or, rather, he repeated at that meeting that I should not stick to municipal borders. If a particular village, a Serb or a Muslim village, wishes to join a neighbouring municipality, it's not going to be a Berlin Wall, so let a particular village join one municipality or the other. And his position was that there should be the smallest possible number of them with us and us with them. That was his position. So that most people should live within their own constituent unit. No one ever referred to any exchange of population. Even Karadzic said that openly, on the 3rd of May, upon his return from Brussels. Asked by a journalist about what was going to happen with the population, whether there was going to be any exchange, somebody mentioned the case of India and Pakistan, I said this is not in our plans and this is not what we recommend. They are going to be a minority and they will have their rights protected on a reciprocal basis. There will be no problem. Now, faced with this marble solid truth, which is well known and easy to prove – one only needs to look at the media reports from that time – which kind of criminal joint enterprise was on the minds of the Serbs? The Serbs had never dishonoured any agreement reached by that time, not even the agreements on truce, as the United Nations’ documents will confirm for you. There were 12 agreements on cease-fire in Sarajevo, 11 of them were breached by the army of the Party of Democratic Action. All of this was happening before the 18th of March, and one can or could assume, at least on the Serbian side, that that was going to be the solution. So based on that, can we draw an inference about the intentions of the Serbs towards eliminating the Muslims and the others from the parts of Bosnia that would not belong to the Serbs? However, my learned friends from the Prosecution are reluctant to put this in the context of the events in the former Yugoslavia and Bosnia in particular because that would then reveal who did what and who was responsible for what. It would become clear that the Serbs were the party that made concessions for the sake of preserving peace and they were never in favour of a war solution for which some other party was. Again, I have to say that this system is devastating and unusual. In the absence of objective judicial investigation, the Prosecution has endless resources to compile the indictment and provide supporting documents. Now, you have a Serb or any person from the Balkan has to appear here and defend himself from some invisible forces, because there is no way for him to carry on his own investigation. But if the Prosecution had conducted an objective investigation, if they had lined up chronologically all that happened in Bosnia and in the Balkans, that chronology would have immediately revealed the true essence. As it is, it turns out, according to the Prosecution, that the war broke out because the accused here set up the Serbian Democratic Party in July 1990 with the intention of getting rid of non-Serbs from the territories that the Serbs in the future, in the uncertain future, would claim, whereas at that point in time Bosnia did not display any secessionist intentions. Well, I can tell you that this was done with a lot of flexibility, creative interpretation and fantasy. This is mentioned in another indictment. In my indictment it says that this was caused by my setting up my party. And in the other indictment it says that the secession of Slovenia on 25 June 1991 was the cause of war. I agree. Croatia declared its independence on the 25th of June, 1995, which led to clashes between the Croatian military forces on the one hand and the JNA, paramilitary and the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina. I don't agree with these paramilitary units, but I agree. Bosnia-Herzegovina declared its independence on the 6th of April, it should be, 1992, which, after 6th of April, 1992, brought about a widespread war. Why do you give up on this truth in my case? ... and names instead something else as the cause of the war. Now, let us hear what a very prominent figure, Professor Cassese, who served as the President of this Tribunal, says: "It is well known that in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, just like in a few former Soviet republics, secession revived old hatreds and brought about terrible bloodshed." Therefore, in my case, according to the OTP, the war was not caused by secession and hatred but rather it was done by Karadzic alone with his impoverished and destitute 1.5 million Serbs in Bosnia, having no allies except God and a few non-influential friendly country. He rose to fight immeasurable forces in a war that was contrary to all Serbian interests, even those interests and objectives, criminal objectives that have been ascribed to us. Not even these objectives could have been achieved through war. Why would the Serbs need war in order to achieve something it already had and wished, and that was to live in Yugoslavia along with all the Muslims, Croats, Slovenes, Macedonians, et cetera? Why did the Serbs need war? They already had what they -- what they wished and that was the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia that can only be preserved in peace. Why would they be against that because this state can only be preserved in peace and will disappear in war. I don't see any reasonable conduct in this context, and I don't see any reason why the Serbs would have done it. Yugoslavia could only have been broken up in war, and this is what is going to be shown here. This is another solid truth that hasn't -- cannot be undermined by anything else. Unlike the Serbs who wanted to preserve Yugoslavia, there were those republics who wanted independence and they could only achieve that through war. There is no doubt about it. Germany not only encouraged that, but they said, "If you continue with the conflicts, we are going to recognise you." But this was also confirmed by our direct war opponents such as President Tudjman, who said that: "There wouldn't have been any war had Croatia didn't want one." And this is what he said at a public rally on a square in May 1991 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: May 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- when the war in Bosnia was already in full flare. I am grateful to Mr. Tudjman and others for what they said and what is going to be useful for my case and I am also grateful for -- to the Prosecution for stretching my responsibility to Croatia as well because that will give me an opportunity to show how all of that looked like and how in 1992 -- 1 and even 1992, column after column of Serbs were arriving who had to flee helter-skelter from those areas because they were being killed there. And on this picture you can see how Bosnia is burning along its edges, but, of course, indeed in the interior part as well. So after the refugees we are seeing shells coming in and the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina became casualties. Let us see who were the people who were killed before the 6th of April. I have been charged for that by the OTP. Those who were casualties before the 1st April were only Serbs, but I'm also grateful to Mr. Izetbegovic for his candour and honesty because he directly relieved me of responsibility when he said in February 1993: "We made our choice, although we could easily have gone another way. The price we paid is high but it had to be paid. If I'm to be blamed for it, then Karadzic should not. We could have avoided this conflict had we remind united as Yugoslavia but we wanted independence. Towards the end of 1991 we established the Patriotic League", and so on... He took it gallantly upon himself, thereby absolving me. Apparently the Prosecution doesn't want to acknowledge this chivalrous attitude of Mr. Izetbegovic. They take everything they get from Izetbegovic as long as it involves a ruse, a trick, deceit, etc. But the chivalrous admission that makes this whole trial quite superfluous – they didn’t even notice. They have a number of corrections for Mr. Izetbegovic. The Patriotic League was not established toward the end of 1991 but, rather, the 31st of March, 1991. During my statement you will see that it was set up two months after we formed a joint government. And a few corrections, but one of them is the most crucial one. The remaining of Bosnia within Yugoslavia and the Bosnian Muslims as well was not the only way to secure peace; it was also possible if we had remained a part of Yugoslavia, while the Muslims and Croats exited according to the West Virginian model. The Lisbon Agreement and the Cutileiro Plan, which envisaged for us, the Serbs, only a small portion of what the Muslims and Croats already had in Bosnia and in the former Yugoslavia: if we had received in Bosnia-Herzegovina only of fraction of that protection and those rights, war could equally have been avoided in that case. The Serbs in Bosnia- Herzegovina would then go to a referendum and give it legitimacy. Peace could have been preserved by holding the referendum on independence. On the eve of the referendum for independence, Radovan Karadzic and Muhamed Cengic, the deputy chairman of the SDA, in the full view of all deputies, reached an agreement for the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina to urgently regionalise the country, that the Serbs go to the referendum to give it legitimacy, but someone from the backbenchers asked Cengic, Who asked you and who authorised you to do this? And you can clearly see Cengic saying, It was Alija Izetbegovic, if you really want to know. So it was Alija Izetbegovic who authorised Muhamed Cengic to offer a solution to the Serbs that would salvage both Bosnia and peace. The Serbs accepted it unconditionally, and in 15 days, an agreement on regionalisation would be adopted. However, some demon forces were at work there that for a hundred times forced Mr. Izetbegovic go back on what he had promised, and after a break, this agreement between Karadzic and Cengic was annulled in front of the whole parliament. Now, another correction relating to Mr. Izetbegovic. Thanks to Serbs' flexibility and numerous concessions that they made, there were several solutions that could have provided the avoidance of war and the price that Mr. Izetbegovic mentioned. However, there was only one solution that inevitably led to war. The Muslim leadership strictly stuck to this solution which could only lead to war, and this solution was sovereign and independent Bosnia, 100 per cent ours. This is the 100 per cent of Bosnia that they actually wanted. This is what they wanted. Then this is what they want now, and this will remain until we have the borders between the entities in Bosnia or we divorce in a peaceful way. They will want it as long as they have a chance. There are some forces that are pressing them and asking them to provide a kind of bridgehead for the interests in Europe. What kind of Serbian joint criminal enterprise could have come into force and be implemented had Mr. Izetbegovic accepted a proposal that was on the table throughout the whole war and which was brought by Mr. Holbrooke in 1995? All these proposals were brought by Stoltenberg and Lord Owen and all other groups. The Serbs accepted all these proposals. Your Excellencies, we had five conferences and five peace plans. I, as the accused, agreed to four of them. So what kind of joint criminal enterprise would be possible had any of the other parties accepted one of the four? And how could the Prosecution come up with the idea at all that the moment we handed over our crisis to the international community to solve it, from then on, there was not a single day without a conference. There was no chance to achieve fait accompli. There was not a chance of uti posidetis juris: what you possess, you shall keep. The solution should have been a political one. Therefore, why would Serbs grab any territories that they cannot verify at any of the conferences and accept it at any of the conferences, and why would the Serbs do anything that then would have to be restored to the previous status? Therefore, how is it possible for the Prosecution not to see that the Serbs accepted everything save for 100 per cent of Bosnia, which would brought us back to the Turkish times when we were a docile people, suffering and trying to preserve their culture through 500 years of unbearable conditions, and I bow to their destiny, and they all deserve that we serve them, because this is something inconceivable. Of course, I have to tell you the Serbs did convert to Islam, but most often based on an agreement between brothers. Then their grandchildren would become enemies. Those who were the first to convert to Islam were not happy about that, but that's how it happened. The brother who did not convert to Islam had to suffer, had to endure pressures and to preserve that, and now it seems that he has to be betrayed by someone and brought back to where he was before. I would like to draw to your attention all the appeals that were sent by prominent Bosniaks to Mr. Izetbegovic for him to change his policy and his behaviour. Let's start with Rabija Subic, a woman from the Muslim circle, but also the president of the Socialist Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That was a multi-ethnic party, with no fundamentalist inclinations. She wrote to Izetbegovic at the beginning of war and she said: "You refused to set up a council of nations. You refused the historic agreement with Serbian people. You refused the Belgrade initiative. Even during Communism we asked for the Council of Nations that could have prevented any war. You rejected an historic agreement with the Serbian people. You refused the Belgrade initiative, and after the summons for the army, on the 4th of April, you started a bloody war." She said: "Immobilise your connections in the Islamic world as well as in Germany and Vatican so they would diplomatically recognise something that was erected by using a political violence. We warn you, Mr. Izetbegovic, that BH independence will be bloody and tragic." In this area there were two municipalities and you will see why this was -- this was possible. This civilised lady, from this multi-ethnic party, correctly perceived the situation and correctly perceived what the solution would be. In similar situations, this was also uttered by Muhamed Filipovic, Nijaz Durakovic, and many others, even some Serbs like Pejanovic, who represents 1.5 Serbs who were in favour of Bosnia without entities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you will be hearing this very often. Please slow down for the benefit of the interpreters. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will. This recollection of the agreement in Bratunac and Vlasenica will initiate the Party of Democratic Action to cancel those meetings. Now, what happened next in Bratunac and Srebrenica, for instance -- I mean, Vlasenica? You're going to hear about that. Srebrenica was, of course, the neighbouring municipality, but you'll hear about Bratunac, then Vlasenica, during this trial, but we could have avoided all that if what Ms. Subic identified as an agreement in those municipalities were respected. And in municipalities throughout Bosnia, negotiations were taking place for the reorganisation of the municipalities and thus avoid tensions, and everybody could see to their own affairs. Now, which Serbian joint criminal enterprise could have been possible at that point in time, if you look at everything that had happened until the letter that the woman wrote to Izetbegovic and what was on the table generally. Now, the Prosecution says that Yugoslavia disintegrated. It fell apart. And that what was needed now -- well, should we actually acknowledge that or was it broken up? Did it disintegrate of itself or was it broken up? Now, the forces that wanted to see the fall of Yugoslavia couldn't have brought it about if there hadn't been influence from outside, and a prime influence, decisive influence. And let's see who said what, what was said by prominent people in the international community about this general matter. "I witnessed at first-hand how Western diplomatic ineptitude and clumsiness hastened the break-up of Yugoslavia and contributed to the dreadful violence and bloodshed that followed the disintegration of the country. Here are a few examples. The premature recognition of Croatia before any guarantees of civil and human rights were given to the Serbian population in Croatia which, because of the horrendous events that occurred there during the Second World War, made civil war inevitable. "The encouragement of Alija Izetbegovic to withdraw his signature from the so-called Lisbon Agreement and proceed with a referendum on independence in Bosnia-Herzegovina, which everyone knew would lead to the death and displacement of thousands of people." James Bissett, the Canadian ambassador to Yugoslavia said that. "The greatest -- biggest mistake was recognising all these little countries when they started to decide they were independent. The Serbs had very good reason to be worried about being in a Muslim-dominated country. It wasn't just paranoia." That was said by Colin Powell, American General. "EC's premature recognition had destroyed the possibility of preventing a global negotiated position for Yugoslavia and contributed to the civil war in Bosnia. The responsibility of Germany and the Vatican for the escalation of the crisis was enormous." That was Ronald Dumas, French foreign minister. "I'm deeply worried that any early selective recognition could widen the present conflict and fuel an explosive situation, especially in Bosnia-Herzegovina." That was Perez de Cuellar. "The prize promised by Genscher had its effect. The Croat separatists intensified their armed activities, blockaded the JNA barracks, their access to water and electricity. The bloodshed went on, and at the year's end, Germany pushed through the recognition of Croatia. Bosnia-Herzegovina, the wonderful small-scale Yugoslavia, was driven into a disastrous civil war lasting several years." Said Ralf Hartmann, the German ambassador to Yugoslavia. "We said if Yugoslavia does not break up peacefully, there's going to be one hell of a civil war. The real problem was that there was a unilateral declaration of independence and a use of force to gain that independence rather than a peaceful negotiation of independence, which is the way it should have happened." Said James Baker, the then US Secretary of State. "The premature recognition of Slovenia and Croat was a guarantee that the break-up of Yugoslavia would not be resolved by peaceful means. Once again, Western intervention had exacerbated and complicated a serious Balkan problem. Again, the German intervention had little to do with the actual problem faced on the ground in Yugoslavia." Said James Bissett, another ambassador, US ambassador. "My view has always been that to have stuck unyieldingly to the internal boundaries of the six republics within the former Yugoslavia before there was any question of any recognition of these republics as being the boundaries for independent states, was a folly far greater than that of premature recognition itself." David Owen, Balkan envoy mediator. "Zimmermann told Izetbegovic the following: Look, why don't you wait and see what the US can do for you, meaning we will recognise you and then help you out, so don't go ahead with the Lisbon Agreement, don't accept the Cutileiro Plan and just hold out for some kind of unitary Bosnian state. So this is a major turning point in our diplomatic efforts." Said George Kenney, an official of the US State Department working on these affairs. Now, I don't know whether to read all these statements or perhaps you can read them on your screens. We have two or three more to go. "Anyway, this kind of American intervention guaranteed civil war in Bosnia and the death of thousands of people, and it acted as if the US had decided to implement a policy which would prevent a solution to the conflict in a way which would not be violent." James Bissett, Canadian ambassador. "The premature recognition of Slovenia, Croatia and Bosnia by the EC and US brought about the war that is going on now." Said Cyrus Vance, US UN envoy. "The German government was pushing for recognition against the resistance of other European countries and the result was a catastrophe." Our host, Ruud Lubbers, the Dutch prime minister. Once when Izetbegovic returned from Germany, he was very sad and said to Professor Koljevic and to myself, that he had received an offer that he couldn't refuse and that he had to move towards independence. Although heavy-hearted, I accused those governments here, of which some were friendly to boot, which set the flames of the third fire in the Balkans in the 20th century. And proof and evidence will show that some of those governments, principally Germany, even while Josip Broz Tito was still alive, had foreseen the outbreak of war and the brutality of that war. The outcome of the war that were advantageous to them, but also not, so they were clairvoyants in a way. And one form of that clairvoyance was one I mentioned, that never was there a war in our country without the civil war component. If you're going to have a war in the Balkans, you're going to have civil war and you'll have brother killing brother. How then can the Prosecution place the responsibilities for the outbreak of a civil war, in the very throes of a civil war which the Western governments and Western services envisaged in this almost clairvoyant way, far before they had ever heard of Karadzic and the Serbian Democratic Party, how can they link it to this accused here and burden him and accuse him for -- of being responsible for all that? The second form of clairvoyance as far as these governments were concerned was that they knew exactly how Yugoslavias came into being and disappeared. This was not the first Yugoslavia nor was it the first disappearance of a Yugoslavia. And if we have time, we'll address that matter in due course, but what I want to tell you is that Yugoslavia was formed and disbanded exclusively following the Western countries' interests when, after World War I, for instance, Serbia as the winning power could decide what Serbia was going to look like, then the Croats and the Slovenes asked to rush into that Serbia and unite. And the West saw a chance for them to get one up on Germany and have Croatia and Slovenia form part of Yugoslavia and reject the Germans from the scene. Now when this was no longer necessary Yugoslavia -- was disintegrated when Germany attacked. When the allies won out, Yugoslavia was reinstated. And when Germany became stronger than the Western powers in 1991, the Yugoslavia disintegrated again and was disbanded, but now, as opposed to 1941, the actors of those Germans' intention were our allies from World War II. And that makes a German victory complete and definite, that their adversaries from World War II were doing -- were doing its work for them. What Germany didn't succeed during World War II when it was defeated, the allies have succeeded now. So those countries are the responsible people. Yugoslavia was just an indicator of the mood and state in Europe and the relationship between Germany and other European countries. It wasn't the intrinsic need of these nations, and let me remind you that before they, for their own interests, pushed the Croats into Yugoslavia in 1918, the Serbs and Croats weren't enemies. There was no reason for them to be enemies at that time. Now let's see what somebody else has to say about the situation or, rather, those forecasts were made during Tito's era. Let's see what Lord Carrington says about the interference of the European Community at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "[Indiscernible] Americans had not intervened in Yugoslavia, there would have been far fewer people killed. There would have been far less ethnic cleansing. There would have been some extremely unhappy and dissatisfied people who felt that they had been done out of their country or their livelihood or whatever it might be, but there was going to be a very large number of dissatisfied and unhappy people at the end of all this. And perhaps the moral of the goal is that you should think very carefully before you intervene in a civil war."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Truth and intelligence always wins in the end, and small nations can only wish to win at the beginning and not later on because later on it's too late. Now I'd like to remind you of this interference of the Western countries not only in influencing the outbreak of the war but also its course, and this was confirmed recently by Richard Holbrooke, Ambassador Richard Holbrooke. And all I can say to him which Njegos, the great poet would have said, thank you very much for that recognition. It will prove correct that certain governments even destroyed all chances for agreements to be reached between the ethnic groups. Now I'd like to skip the part relating to the Assembly. The interpreters have asked me to speak slower. Now, Mr. Tieger, my respected adversary, in his opening statement says even at first glance at the documents from the October session, for example, the Assembly session on the 15th of October which was a crucial Assembly and a crucial decision taken about the future of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that even a cursory glance at the transcript of the Assembly meeting proves Serb responsibility and Serb culpability, but I think that this cursory glance is our problem here. The Defence is opposed to having any superficial view of this question, and it will do everything in its power to avoid this superficiality but go into the substance. Now, the text that you see on your screen is a session at which the SDA party finally managed, in an unconstitutional and illegal way, to pass the declaration on sovereignty without any Serb Assembly members and without the Speaker of the Parliament who had concluded the session, and they convened a new meeting without the right to do so. So all the barriers in avoiding constitutionality and legality were broken down. I delivered a speech at the Assembly which is the most exploited speech ever by the Prosecution. And I think that's the worst thing that they can say of me and hold against me, whereas, Your Excellencies, that speech is an antiwar speech, very much so, in which the Serb side -- or, rather, I am entreating that we opt for variants for peace and I'm offering all manner of concessions. Now, if the Defence is given the opportunity of presenting all the relevant data and evidence, you will be able to see that what happened on the ground, in the chaos of civil war, to that was added mass killing of one's own population, mass crimes in the centre of Sarajevo, the bread line at Vasa Miskin, the crime at the stadium, Markale 1 and 2. These are all amazing examples and twists and innovations of slyness applied in war, and the actors thereof are proud of that. Now, if we reject what Mr. Tieger says, a cursory glance, superficial glance of the material we have concerning the Markale incident, we can see what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a normal market day at Markale, when there are a lot of sellers, a lot of goods at the market to be sold. Now, this is another picture before the alleged explosion of the Serb mine. It is the 5th of February, 1994, in the afternoon. This is a leg, artificial limb, which allegedly was blown off by a Serb mine from somebody, but it's a prosthetic. There are no people in the marketplace, no fruit and vegetables being sold, whereas 3 or 400 people are supposed to have been there and many of them hit by shells allegedly. And here we have that same artificial limb as having been blown off by a Serb shell. Now, look at the tables. There's nothing on them. No goods are being sold. It's a dark, winter's afternoon, an unpleasant place. Nobody there, and 3 or 400 people suddenly appeared there. What were they doing there? How does the Prosecutor expect experienced Judges to accept this plot or planting of evidence? We will see in the courtroom -- here you have the corpses of the killed -- of killed fighters who they scattered around for their purposes. This killed soldier was brought in a plastic foil and then taken away in this state, rigor mortis had already set in. You see that there are no goods on the stalls. Let us hear what he has to say. "I want to introduce myself. I am Colonel Demurenko. I am Chief of Staff, Sector Sarajevo. I want explain any details of investigations which was provided UN, so-called UN expertise. As a professional man, I cannot agree with argument of UN specialist about reasons and sources of this shelling. This is a material -- maybe one portion of whole material of UN specialist about the shelling, but it was very strange conclusion, include idea about the shelling was from Serbian side. Small picture which explained angle. This is a direction of fire. This is place of explosion, and in accordance with investigation, direction of fire was 176 degrees. "Today, personally, with my special -- not special, very small investigation group including [indiscernible] officers, we was to this place, this place, this, this and this, we went on foot and I can affirm absolutely without -- beyond any doubts this is place unacceptable or unsuitable for firing position mortar shell. "For conclusion of material of investigation was wrong. Now I said only about terrain where is located Serbian troops. They investigate only angles and directions and automatically thinking about Serbian so-called aggressions against civil population in Sarajevo, but I think it's -- it's not correct. "Let's stop them, stop false and falsehood and lie about Serbian aggressions in this area, please. Or investigate it absolutely correctly with full argumentation or stop it."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, whenever you find it convenient.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me, I would just like to state my views on this particular matter. This is a war trick, a display of cunning in war which led to the punishment of the Serbs as a warring party. They say that all is fair in love and war. I don't think that all is fair either in love or in war, but it is certain that in war these kind of things happen, but is this permissible in a courtroom, in a court of law? How does the Prosecution dare to proffer this to you as if it were the truth? And there is not a single element, there is not a single marksman who can shoot this way, who can, with just one mortar shell – and that is indirect fire - hit that market in this way. There are no people there. There are no goods in the market, and all of a sudden two hundred people turn up injured, or – let’s say - at least one hundred are not hit. Did those market stalls protect anyone? I think that this is the supreme injustice that happened in this court of law. It is the supreme injustice because it's against truth and justice. However, the Prosecution is continuing this war trickery and they bring this in to convict a general to life in prison. This was the trial of General Galic. And now they are trying to convict me of the same thing as his supreme commander for something that we never did. The -- one Trial Chamber already passed this kind of judgement. However, the OTP convinced five Appeals Judges that this was a crime committed by the Serbs. What is an even greater crime is to convince the Muslim masses that this is what the Serbs had done to them. How can one hope for reconciliation between the Serbs and Muslims if the Muslims are to believe that the Serbs did this to them? And we are going to prove that the Serbs never did this to the Muslims. We are going to prove in this courtroom that Serbs never did this. Excellencies, I believe that that will do as far as the opening statement is concerned with regard to this particular incident, but I do have to draw your attention to these war tricks, that the OTP simply took over and continues along those lines as if the war were not over. In this way, the OTP becomes a participant in the war, and they are trying to draw this Chamber and this Tribunal into a war that seems to be ongoing in that way. If this is convenient, we can take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me, but if I could raise one potential point of clarification before you break very quickly. My earlier request in connection with a cautionary measure, that is the motion filed on February 13th, I believe, was not about a warning - excuse me - to the accused concerning the continuance of trial, which was the earlier subject, but instead to the motion for an instruction regarding admissibility of submissions. It may well have been understood but I wanted to clarify that because the Court's reference to previous discussion caused me some concern that the Bench may have been thinking I was referring to the possibility of a warning about continuance rather than the motion for an instruction regarding the admissibility of statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Admissibility of submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of submissions instead, Your Honour, yes. And that was a motion filed on February 23rd. I believe the Defence responded by indicating they had no position on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll take a look over the break. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, we looked at the motion you referred to, and the Chamber found it sufficient to note that this stage that it is pursuant to Rule 84 that the accused is making his statement, and then the remainder will be taken care of after his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour, and I wasn't disputing the Court in any way. I just was concerned about the possibility of some confusion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like us to have a look at what Lord Owen says, who was a mediator in the search for peace. Let us see what he says about Markale.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Lord Owen, formerly head of the British diplomacy, represents Europe as a Co-Chairman of the Conference on the former Yugoslavia, together with Mr. Stoltenberg, representative of the United Nations. [Voiceover] On the evening of the 12th of February, the twelve foreign ministers received reports, which was photocopied for me, specifically paragraph 7 which is related to the Sarajevo assassination on the 5th of February. Lord Owen wrote, I quote: 'The position from which this shell was launched is located one and a half kilometre deep into the Muslim-held territory, measured from the demarcation line which separates this territory from the Army of Republika Srpska.'"

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will see, Excellencies, in this courtroom, a multitude of similar things that the other side did to their own people, that were stage managed. Now I'd like to draw your attention to yet another trick of this sort that caused serious damage to us there and now the Prosecution is trying to benefit from it even further.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "Anybody pretending that there are innocents in this business, and that there is one side that is pure white, the victims, and other side pure-on black, the aggressors. That is not the case. "Lord David Owen came to Bosnia-Herzegovina in August of 1992 to replace Lord Carrington as mediator for the European Community and with a reputation as a hard-line critic of the Bosnian Serbs. But Owen quickly learned that Muslim forces routinely staged incidents to turn world opinion against the Serbs. Media reports, for instance, had accused the Serbs of targeting Kosevo Hospital in Sarajevo. "The UN monitors actually saw a mortar bomb, a mortar crew come into the hospital in Bosnian government military forces uniform and fire over the Kosevo Hospital into an area, presumably Serb. And all of it was packed up very quickly. A television crew arrived, set up on the grounds of the hospital. A few minutes later, retaliatory fire from the place where the mortar came and, of course, landed on the hospital, all filmed on television. "Owen learned a strongly worded letter had been sent to the government of Alija Izetbegovic by the UN commander in Sarajevo, General Filip Morillon, stating: 'I now have concrete evidence from witnesses of this disreputable and cowardly act. I must point out to you the harm that such blatant disregard for the Geneva Convention does to your cause.' "When I said to General Morillon, who is, I think, an exceptionally able soldier in every way, Why don't you make this public? He shrugged his shoulder in a sort of Gallic way and he said, You have to look at it." "Lord Owen and UN mediator Cyrus Vance found that their efforts to negotiate a compromise to end the conflict were undermined by the propaganda war that targeted US public opinion. "In America they have a press and a television presentation that is still cowboys and Indians, good and bad. They like to see things in simple terms. There's no doubt about that, and it's been helped by some very strongly motivated propaganda. It's a propaganda war as well as an actual physical war."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. What His Lordship said was a propaganda war, as he had put it, and this propaganda war could not have been waged and all of this cunning could not have been something that the Serbs would be blamed for if there weren't for the assistance of all of those who were there on behalf of the international community. You will see in this courtroom, in due course, to what a low level humanitarian organisations stooped, even some who had a perfectly good name until then. There were some that were without borders indeed before, but they destroyed the very essence of the idea of being humanitarian. They were spying for one of the warring parties. They lied in press releases. They smuggled arms and ammunition, and they also crossed our lines, pretending to belong to these organisations and protected vehicles, and later when our soldiers became suspicious and started checking them, then we are criticised for being unpleasant to these organisations. They smuggled weapons. They smuggled enemy combatants. In a word, they were a warring party. They were a warring party. When our troops legitimately started defending themselves from these sabotage actions, these unlawful actions launched by certain organisations, humanitarian organisations that were doing this either on their own or were simply handing their vehicles, their protected vehicles over to others, we had this dirty war waged against us. And also there was the war in the media, as Lord Owen said, that could not have happened if it weren't for the media. You will see during this period of time -- or, rather, during these proceedings, that false journalists ruined the idea of journalism, of impartial journalism, how these false journalists led to the death of true journalists in many theatres of war throughout the world because they destroyed the very idea of the impartiality of journalism, and they abused this sacred duty or this sacred position of being impartial and of not being a warring party and that thereby they should have open access everywhere, just as we did for them. For example, there was a British TV crew that we brought on our own plane after the London conference. We brought them there, and we allowed them to go wherever they wanted to go. And then there was this other Markale in 1992, from Trnopolje. You will see that footage and you will prove -- and we will prove that Trnopolje was not a camp. Rather, it was a collection centre that was run by the refugees themselves. This is how that picture with barbed wire appeared and was broadcast all over the world.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "[Previous translation continues] Trnopolje village. The centre was used by people in transit. They were trying to get away from the fighting and needed a place to stay during their travels."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] I had to come here. Those that did not fight came here. "We have nothing to fight for. I came with children, young children, here down the field. Nobody harassed us. Nobody laid a finger on us. I stayed in the village. "[Previous translation continues] [In English] ... centre of Trnopolje included a medical facility. The Yugoslav and ITN crews interviewed Dr. Mestrinic Idriz [phoen], a Muslim doctor there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] We have been here from the very first day. People came here of their own free will, probably because of food shortages." "[In English] Ms. Marshall chose not to set up her cameras and film in this open area. Instead, she and her crew manoeuvred into a partly enclosed space used as a storage area for wheelbarrows and the like. The dilapidated fence had chicken wire on the bottom, a few strands of barbed wire on top to discourage theft. Our crew filmed the ITN people as they manoeuvred into this area through a hole in the broken-down fence. Someone in front of the crowd of refugees said, Here, this one speaks English, pointing to Mr. Mehmet [phoen]. "I think it's very [indiscernible] nothing wrong here. "Do you feel safe here? "I think it's very safe but it's very hard. "Here's a little diagram showing the position of the two crews. The ITN people are the blue circle on the left; we are the red circle on the right. "This man is very thin. "Penny Marshall had set up her cameras behind barbed wire. She was in position. Now she searched the crowd for that perfect look. She wanted a star for her story. The story she would sell the world."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, we will prove by way of evidence that the Prosecution has been trying to use against us, through that we are going to prove what we are trying to say. This was a collection centre. This was a transit point for persons who had nowhere to go because of the combat going on around them. This will tellingly be proved by the evidence that the Prosecution is trying to use against us, but we are going to use it in our own defence. The team that you saw went into the tool shed, and there's barbed wire around it. So they were surrounded by barbed wire, but they were filming free people, and we suffered gravely on account of the fact that this image went all over the world. We were harshly punished for that imagery. I wonder how Ms. Penny Marshall sleeps after all the harm she inflicted on us by sending these images around the world, but to have this brought into court and to have this war cunning be used in a court of law and to create a picture of the Serbs on that basis and to condemn the Serbs on that basis, that is a different matter. I have said that we had done everything possible to achieve peace and avoid war. Let me remind you that in 1991 there was a lot of tension. There was war in Croatia. There were misunderstandings. Then this junior MBO, Muslim party led by Zulfikarpasic and Filipovic, came to see us and said, This is bad, what's going on is not good. Are you going to give up on the idea of regionalisation of Serb autonomous provinces and all other measures that we undertook exclusively as a response to the measures undertaken against us by the SDA and we did accept, and this is what one of their leaders testified about this. They designed and proposed an historic Serb-Muslim agreement with a view to avoiding war, and the whole idea was to have the Muslims and the Serbs living alongside each other. If that had happened, we would know how many of them would still have been alive and how many of them would not have been living in poverty had this agreement been accepted. And as I said, all the measures that we have employed in response to illegal measures undertaken by the Muslim and the Croat side were based in law and international covenants. However, we abandoned all that once Zulfikarpasic and Filipovic came up with this idea. Now is a good time to point to an illusion that the Prosecution wants to create, because this -- without this kind of illusion and trick they cannot indict me. They claim that Serbs do not wish to live with the Muslims. On the other hand, we were doing everything possible to keep Muslims in Yugoslavia. The Serbs wanted to live with Muslims, but they didn't want to live under the Muslims, and this is our right. We shall never live under this kind of regime that would deprive us of our fundamental rights. So once we have established that the Serbs did everything to keep the Muslims in Yugoslavia and to live with them, the indictment should fall. For some time they would have been in the second place. Soon, perhaps, they would have been in the first place. But they would have had protection. What would the Muslims have in this kind of Yugoslavia? They would enjoy the protection as a people, and they would enjoy the protection in their own republic. If the Muslims said, "We want to leave Yugoslavia," we would just tell them, "Give us what you have in Yugoslavia, give us our own constituent unit in Bosnia, and we can leave." As I said, 100 per cent of power in 100 per cent of Bosnia was never an option. Now, if you take only one sentence from one speech, and I'm talking about my speech that was very much exploited, I would like to draw to your attention to this speech and this -- I would like to assess it. It was delivered on the 15th of October, and it relates to a definitive and forcible adoption of the declaration on independence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Because what you are proposing impinges on the integrity of Yugoslavia and the integrity of Yugoslavia can be disrupted in the federal parliament, I'm not sure even of that, but it can be if you come to an agreement in the federal parliament and other federal institutions. Many plans get mixed here. You referred to the constitution and the laws when it suits you; and when it doesn't suit you, you come out political proclamations. Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina can prevent Croats and Muslims, if necessary, from getting out of Yugoslavia, but we will not prevent you. We will not do that because we are a sovereign people. Gentleman, I did not come here as a god of war, which is how somebody from the Croatian Democratic Party named me, but I want to repeat, for the hundredth time, that the Serbian Democratic Party does not create the will of the Serbian people. It interprets it. We would lie to you if we said that you can adopt this and that you can do something with this in Europe. "Gentlemen from the SDA, for the last three months we've been talking about other rights. We are talking freely and openly about a different way of organising Bosnia and Herzegovina, where some kind of a three-tier approach will enable Bosnia to stay united and Serbs, Muslims and Croats to stay in Yugoslavia for as long as they want to. This is a three-tier solution where the sovereignty of the peoples, as Mr. Bjelobrk correctly said, would be exercised not only at the level of the republic and the federal state but also in autonomous provinces. If you don't want this, we could agree with you leaving Yugoslavia by means of a plebiscite, but we shall use the same mechanism to prevent you from taking us out of Yugoslavia. We do not mind if you submit an initiative to change the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But you cannot do it this way. It has to be done through the constitutional commission, civil council of citizens which is where we would then vote. "I'm trying to tell you, in the calmest way possible, the Serbian people know what you want. You want to tell the people in The Hague that this is a third or fourth republic that does not want to live in Yugoslavia, but you cannot do that because we want to live in Yugoslavia. You can say that in your name. All the sovereign people in Bosnia can only speak for themselves. They cannot speak for other peoples. We have reached that conclusion in this parliament. Before the national and international public, we will prevent you from committing violence, constitutional violence against Serbs because the constitutional violence breeds all other kinds of violence. We will not be in control anymore. This has been repeated here a hundred times. We will no longer be in control if we get into a situation where Croatia and Slovenia are, especially Croatia. The hell would be a thousand times worse in Bosnia-Herzegovina. There would be no way to stop it. "I ask you once again, I am not threatening, I am pleading that you take seriously the political will of the Serbian people represented here today, the Serbian Democratic Party, the Serbian Renewal Movement and some Serbs from the other parties represent. I plead with you to fully understand that what you are doing is not good. The road that you are choosing for Bosnia and Herzegovina is the same highway to hell and suffering that Slovenia and Croatia have already taken. Do not think that you will not take Bosnia and Herzegovina to hell and the Muslim people maybe into extinction, because if there is a war, the Muslim people will not be able to defend themselves. "Please, these are big statements, but serious situations demand big statements. How are you going to prevent people in Bosnia and Herzegovina from killing each other? How can the war in Croatia be prevented, especially in areas where Serbs and Croats live together and where their political wills have clashed without adhering to the legal framework which is the only way to resolve."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also said we have to prevent chaos from setting in. We can introduce order. We have it in our hands. But we cannot manage chaos. So taking this all into consideration and having heard what exceptional authorities worldwide said about the recognition and other issues, we have to ask ourselves what this small community of Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina could do except surrender and annihilate themselves. Therefore, we have an opportunity here to make a distinction between whether this was lawful conduct on the part of the HDZ and the SDA and the Serbs were violating their rights, or whether it was vice versa. They were in breach and the Serbs tried to defend themselves to a minimum, by making endless concessions. You saw that the constitution was violated when and if necessary, and then this kind of brokered constitution is being revoked, which is impossible. Now, the Croatian writer Krleza said that this crisis developed by making a comparison with this picture: You turn off the light in the Balkan tavern, and after everything is over, you turn the lights back on. The Serbs couldn't allow that to happen. Let me remind you that the division and the partition of Bosnia and Herzegovina came from outside, and that was primarily the idea of Mr. Izetbegovic. This will be confirmed by all his associates and by this intercept that you are going to hear. He was only interested in having Bosnia-Herzegovina, albeit a small one, but with Arab and Muslim influence in it. Can we now please listen to this conversation between Karadzic and Milosevic, which is not intended for the public to hear, where they speak to each other very candidly and authentically.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
