utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Karadzic: They surprised us the day before yesterday, after that lunch. They completely took us by surprise. Izetbegovic talked about the division of Bosnia, explicitly and openly, he'd never been more explicit. We were shocked. We hadn't thought about that. I don't think he (Izetbegovic) wants to unite with Croatia. He wants to use Croatia to leave Yugoslavia, because what he'd like is to have some Islamic enclave in the valley of the River Bosna, which I think he needs for the Arab world. We still believe that it would be a pity if Bosnia were to fall apart. That is our basic stand. "Milosevic: Not all Muslims will do what Alija Izetbegovic is doing. I am sure. "Karadzic: He is very cunning. He doesn't speak what those ultimate moves are. Those last moves of his, the last intentions of an Islamic republic, and he is hiding behind the state and citizens."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, having had insight into all of this, the Prosecution is trying to characterise me as a leader who formulated and implemented this criminal plan of creating a separate ethnic entity comprising large territories of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This did not happen until we were forced to take what was offered to us just to save our lives. They said Karadzic was the ultimate leader. If they knew the Serbian people properly, they would have said that Karadzic was the ultimate servant of his people, and this is what you can find in -- in the Gospels. The second part of the sentence is not only disputable but it's also untrue, and it's similar to the one in -- proffered by the Prosecution in paragraph 11, where it says: "As Yugoslavia disintegrated, republics moved toward independence." This is very cunning. I have to give them credit for that. The republics moved toward independence because Yugoslavia was disintegrating. I would like to recommend to all of you, as a kind of entertainment, everything that the Prosecution says against me just turn it around. You will see it's more correct and true and it's very entertainment. We have to reverse this upside logic. In that case, this paragraph would sound as follows: When the republics moved towards independence, that is when Yugoslavia started disintegrated. And this is what the truth is, not what the OTP is saying. The first step was for the republics who proclaimed unlawful, illegal, unilateral secessions, and we heard it from a very prominent expert. However, the OTP here is trying to convince you this took place the other way around, and, of course, in that context you can't speak about the Serbs' blame. However, if it is clear that the independence of republics caused the disintegration, then everything becomes clear, let alone the fact that Yugoslavia did not break up, did not disintegrate, but it was broken up from the outside. Bosnia was fragmented, and Yugoslavia was broken up. How could Bosnia embark on the road towards -- towards independence without the Serbs and against the Serbs’ will? If you look at the maps and the areas where the Serbs have been living for ages, you will understand that we’re going to prove here that the SDA didn't need the Bosnian Serbs but they, rather, needed their territories, the two-third territories of Bosnia. The OTP said that the Serbs constituted one-third of the population, but we shall come to that, how it happened that the Serbs who had always been majority became only one-third, but that one-third of population lived on two-thirds of the territory in Bosnia-Herzegovina. If the SDA had wanted the Serbian territories, it could have been available to the OTP in the form of one very strong proof thanks to Mr. Tudjman with whom I had a lot of conversations. Let us now listen to an intercept between Tudjman and a high delegation from the US in which he said, Muslims told me once that they were going to exterminate them all, talking about the Serbs. I asked them, How are you going to expel one and a half million Serbs out of Bosnia? And then Tudjman says, Although the Muslim leadership is not unified, they cannot count on a war that will end with the expulsion of the Serbs but they, rather, have to rely on Croatia, and sooner or later the Serbs would leave Bosnia. I have been accused here of wanting the Muslims to leave Republika Srpska. The Muslims that they are referring to, the SDA Muslims, the young Muslims, the fundamentalists, wanted all the Serbs to leave Bosnia. And now we see just how sincere Mr. Izetbegovic was, the president of the SDA, and his moves, when he said, If I am to be accused of that, then you don't have to accuse Karadzic. And at one point in time I take it upon myself, liberating me of all responsibility. Now, President Tudjman protected Mr. Izetbegovic during the war. We didn't want his defeat, but we did want to see his political defeat and his political idea of having 100 per cent power and 100 per cent Bosnia. So this is a completely authentic piece of evidence. The Prosecution then moves on and follows the same erroneous path when it says in one of its paragraphs that Karadzic took part in negotiations aiming to create a joint state and simultaneously prepared organs and conditions for the forcible ethnic separation and creation of a Serb state carved out from Bosnia and Herzegovina similar to a process that had started in Croatia. What kind of joint state when the joint state already existed, I ask you. Now, further on in another paragraph, the Prosecution goes on to say that the Serbs in Croatia, because they're now linking us up, have this earmarked territories considered Serb, created separate Serb institutions to resist Croatian authority, declared autonomy and then independence, and forcibly took control of approximately one-third of Croatian territory. Well, this is how it was. We saw that the Croatian secession was illegal, unlawful, and this illegality the Serbs resisted, and that is legitimate. But as far as the Prosecution is concerned, it's not legitimate. Now, because of things of this kind, the Prosecution seems to be a porte-parole of my wartime adversaries rather than a Prosecution in this Tribunal. No legal instance or scholarly or scientific forum ever established that Croatia acted lawfully and that the Serbs did not have the right to put up a resistance to that illegality. Let me remind you what happened to the Serbs in Croatia. The Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina are the oldest population there. All the territory was theirs. The Serbs came to Croatia 300 or 350 years ago and they were given Krajina not from Croatia but from Austro-Hungary. Austria, in fact, and they were fighters there and they were given privileges as such, autonomous rights were accorded to them. They were given the territory. If, in 1918, the Serbs in Krajina had been told that one day they would have to leave this joint state and be in Croatia, live in Croatia, Krajina would not have been a part of Croatia, and maybe not even Croatia would have been part of Yugoslavia, and we would still be friends. Or if in 1945, the population in Krajina were told that the Croatia that they were entering would one day be taken away from them and that they would been expelled, Krajina would not be in Croatia at all. So the people of Krajina were tricked. They were given Krajina from Austria because they earned it by fighting and defending the whole of Europe from the Turkish onslaught and invasion and then they entered then Croatia, when in 1945 they entered Croatia and took in the dowry that Croatia was. Then it said in the constitution that Croatia was two-nation state, a state of Croats and Serbs; whereas in 1991, the first thing that the HDZ did in Croatia was to throw the Serbs out of the constitution and turn them into a national minority so that they could then seize Krajina away from them. Now we can see what Professor Antonio Cassese, whom you all know well, says about these unlawful steps taken by Croatia for which the Prosecution maintains that the Serbs cannot resist in Krajina, as if those steps had been lawful. The Prosecution is accusing me of ethnocentrism of some kind, and it says that we were ethnically motivated in wishing to create our own territories both in Croatia and in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Please, exclusively ethnic motives were on the side of the Slovenes, Croats and Muslims to step down from Yugoslavia. They weren't political motives or economic ones or racial or religious ones. They were purely ethnic motives that led them to do that. Whereas the Serbs are being denied their right at the onslaught of other interests to protect their own interests. So ethnic -- all possible crises after World War II were ethnically motivated, especially from 1968 to 1971 in Croatia, when Tito replaced the whole Croatian leadership ethnically. Karadzic, after 1968, no longer delved in politics. He took part in the student movement and then was a sort of dissident and worked in his profession and not in politics. So ethnic nationalism in 1990 and 1991 brought about everything that happened later on, whereas the Serbs are held responsible. Let me remind you that in Croatia the Serbs did not vote for the Serbian Democratic Party in the majority but for a multi-ethnic party of Ivica Racan, of the Communists of Ivica Racan. Croatia had many parties and many secessionist parties at that, but the Croats voted for the HDZ, the most ethnically coloured one; whereas the Serbs voted for the least ethnically coloured party that cannot be considered Serb at all, and those Serbs in Croatia are then accused in the package and all of us together with them by the Prosecution that we were ethnocentric or goodness knows what else. Now, if we have time, I would like to show you what it is that the Serbs in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, because Bosnia-Herzegovina during World War II was joined to Croatia, what they could expect. We're going to see something about Jasenovac, which is just across the Sava River from us, and this is what the Wiesenthal Centre says. The Ustashas founded in 1930, according to the centre, killed 500.000 Serbs, expelled 250.000 and the others were converted. So that's Mile Budak's theory of the three thirds, a Croatian writer and ideologue. We're going to expel a third, kill a third and convert a third. And when a Serb in Bosnia-Herzegovina says this as an allegory, as tit for tat, the Prosecutor says and places in the indictment that this is the Serb position. But it's common knowledge that there will be three thirds. However, the Prosecutor does not have good advisors on the ground so that they can be told and explained what a reported speech actually means. Now, this is what the German -- is this still Wiesenthal on our screens? Let's see what a German intelligence officer says. And I'd like to draw Your Excellencies 'attention to the fact that up until the 17th of February, 1942, there was a very precise estimation made by a German intelligence officer, according to which up until then 300.000 Orthodox Serbs had already been killed, butchered, using -- applying sadistic methods. Now this figure could not have decreased. It could only have increased. It only began to decrease when the Communists came into power. It became smaller and smaller until they reached a figure of 80.000, as if 80.000 were a small figure. But the -- Croatia was ready to acknowledge the 80.000, but it is certain that there were more than 500.000 because if in one year it was 300.000, then the number could have only increased with each passing year. And the Wiesenthal Centre claims that about a million Serbs from Croatia and Bosnia were in fact killed. Now, what I'm being accused of by the Prosecution in their false indictment I would like to turn round and create into a truthful indictment, where everything stays the same but the actors change. Instead of the Serb leaders, the Croatian and Muslim leaders would stand accused, and the places would be reversed too. And let's see what that would look like. Genuine indictment. As if Tudjman or Izetbegovic in -- from 1990 to 1995, led the formulation and implementation of a criminal plan to create an ethnic entity on large portions of the FRY of Yugoslavia. Or Tudjman, Izetbegovic, engaged in negotiations to secure a common state, and they did indeed, while simultaneously preparing the organs, entities and conditions for the forcible ethnic separation and creation of a Croat Muslim state carved out from Yugoslavia similar to a process that had started in Slovenia -- or, rather, in Croatia vis-a-vis Bosnia-Herzegovina. Furthermore, paragraph 13, everything is the same -- remains the same but we changed the actors. Croats, Muslims earmarked territories considered Croat Muslim, created separate Croat or Muslim institutions to resist Yugoslav authority, declared independence and forcibly took control of a large part of Yugoslav territory, and the Yugoslav population did not accept those decisions on that territory. Now, Your Excellencies in the Trial Chamber and gentlemen in the various governments and the Prosecution that supports this process of taking the Serbs to trial, my variations of these paragraphs in the pre-trial brief of the Prosecution is far more believable and far more exact than the Prosecutor's. To this paragraphs we should add that these leaders of the Croats and Muslims, and they can't accuse us of that, that they worked to set up secret republican armies, services, armed themselves, violated United Nations Resolutions, had plans to revive the empire Croatia, and the Western Europe countries would like to reinstate the Habsburg Monarchy. And you will see how the Muslim population in Turkey would like to see Turkey return to the Balkans, which allegedly during the Turkish occupation of 500 years, flourished and was stable. Yes, it was stable, just like a cemetery is stable. Nobody does anything there. There is no movement at all in a cemetery. But Serbian culture which until the arrival of the Turks was the leading culture in real Europe, and Stefan Lazarevic was the leader, leading figure, he was a poet, he was a hero, well liked by his friends in Europe, all this stopped when Turkey arrived. Now Turkey wants – from the mouth of the most responsible individuals from 1990 on, from Turgut Ozal, and Minister Davutoglu – that Bosnia is Turkish and Turkey is Bosnian. We are one and we will come back again because it is in our interest to revive the Ottoman Empire. That is something that the Serbs do not accept. If I had more time, I would produce a series of evidence to show that the rhythm of the terrible changes in Croatia immediately after the elections, what happened. Every month there was a new shocking measure against the Serbs. First of all, the amendment throwing them out of the constitution. Then the constitution itself in which they were reduced to a national minority. Then you had other measures that were taken. Arming secretly. Then next we had expulsions, killings in towns and in Serbian territories where the Serbs were in the majority, and so then we had -- already had columns of refugees. People were sacked from their jobs. And the Prosecution knows this full well and they have uttered it in -- we have heard testimony about that from witnesses in these various courtrooms. I was personally able to see what those refugees looked like in those columns. President Tudjman rehabilitated the NDH, Independent State of Croatia. He was not a Ustasha. He was a partisan. But the Ustashas took power, they occupied leading positions in the land, and everything resulted, already in 1991, with a vast number of refugees whom we took in in Bosanska Krajina and Banja Luka. Now the Prosecution wants to say that that had no effect and influence on the state of mind of the Bosnian Serbs, that they could see the heads of the wealthiest houses in Europe lying on the floor of a sports hall with nothing left, no villages, no past, no present, no future. And one of those measures was to introduce Ustasha symbols straight away, Ustasha insignias taken over from the previous Ustasha state, and the Prosecution thinks that that is of no importance. And let's see what Lord Owen has to say on the subject, just how important that was. "It was extremely provocative," he says, "for the Serbs in Croatia that Tudjman's government had adopted the independent Croatian NDH flag with the same symbol used by Pavelic, the red and white chequer-board. And it is under these insignias that the million Serbs suffered and fell as fatalities in World War II." That is what His Lordship says. These are lucid and accurate observations from his Lordship, but with a little addendum. It wasn't provocative only, it was terrifying, both for the Serbs and for the Jews. And it corresponds to the title of a book written by Goldstein, a Croatian Jew: 1941, The Year That Is Returning. But the Prosecution says, Don't pay any attention to any insignias. It is just a gesture, nothing stands behind it. Let's see precisely what stands behind it, and for that, let us see what the minister says, Ministers Spegelj and Boljkovac say on subject, the minister of defence and the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] There are 9.000 JNA officers and 18.000 JNA soldiers on the whole territory of the Fifth Military District: Slovenia, Croatia and part of Bosnia. We have now 80.000 people armed with Kalashnikovs. We will resolve Knin in the way that we will butcher them. We have the international community, especially now when this whore has won in Serbia. [INTERLOCUTOR] Milosevic? Yes. Now, two days after he had won, the Americans offered to help us, and up until then they had only speculated they would -- they said, Now it will be like this, 1.000 armoured vehicles, cars, who knows what else. They will provide weapons and equipment for 100.000 soldiers, all free of charge."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we hearing interpretation? Can you stop the video.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Why it is not translated?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that they don't have the transcript and what is being now --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: That should be live translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: -- said has already been translated --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Those words --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: -- before.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Those words of Minister Spegelj are repeated here clearly and should be translated live, simultaneously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it that what we heard is the interpretation of what just heard now. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Free of charge. The army has no business there. They will be massacred. Everybody will be massacred already in their homes. To kill on the spot, on the street, in the army barracks compound, anywhere. Just take a pistol and shoot in the stomach. This will not be a conventional war. It will be a civil war with no consideration towards anyone. Not even towards women or not children. The bombs simply need to be thrown into family apartments. "Physical liquidation. Somebody enters the apartment, the courier, he appears in front of the door, bang, bang, bang, and returns downstairs. Let them call the police to establish who was that. Then down the stairs he goes to the other and kills him at the same time. Don't mind the women or the children. It does not matter. "We will use all means. We will also weapons. Serbs will never again be in Croatia as long as we are here."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please believe me, Your Excellencies, that they did all this and worse. Everything they announced at the end of 1990, when they were deep in Yugoslavia still, they were within Yugoslavia. Whereas they had prepared part of their population, the Serb population, they had prepared massacres for them and they carried that out ultimately. And what was promised at the time just as, for example, at the inauguration of the Party of Democratic Action - Dalibor Brozovic said that Croatia would defend itself along the Drina River, as was the case in World War II. Or like some hapless Sime Djodan, of Serb origin, Croatian extremist, said that on a Serb mountain overlooking Sarajevo, the chequer-board flag would be hoisted in five years' time. Well, we didn't believe that that would happen but in five years' time, yes, indeed, there was a complete repetition of what happened during World War II and the columns of persons who were expelled, and you saw those columns leaving and fleeing Croatia. All of that is accessible to the Office of the Prosecutor and to the entire world. Everyone knows when this happened, how it ended, and what the authentic story is. However, the Prosecution claims that it is I who watched what was happening to the Serbs in Croatia, and that on that basis, I warned the Bosnian Serbs, mobilised them, told them to defend themselves and so on. So it is without reason, without foundation that I disturbed the Krajina Serbs and taught the Bosnian Serbs, as their leader, what could happen to them and what they should do in order to prevent that from happening to them. The OTP says that this had no basis, but really, this pre-trial brief against me would have to be better or there should have been no indictment against me in the first place. If grenades, shrapnel, streams of refugees and promises from the minister of defence and the minister of the interior in Croatia are not a danger for Serbs in Croatia and Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina, that means that we should have been in a deep state of anaesthesia and that we should have waited to be butchered like the Serbs before us. This is how the OTP qualifies this. Now, if we were to turn it the other way round just by switching names and protagonists, this is the genuine indictment. Karadzic and the Bosnian Serb leadership were aware of the nature and purpose of Croat arming campaign, the creation of an illegal army through creating an illegal army and an enormous police force, dismissals of Serbs from work on ethnic grounds, killing of Serbs in towns, illegal degradation of Serbs constitutional status. They knew that Croatian Serbs were living in fear because of the return of Ustasha emigres and their appointment to official positions; because of the unstoppable preparations for Croatia’s unilateral secession from Yugoslavia; because of the future position of the Serbs after secession in that republic, which was already hinting what that position would be by changing the Constitution to the Serbs’ detriment. Karadzic supported the efforts by Krajina Serbs to protect their existence and cited them as an example to the Bosnian Serbs in case Bosnia chooses the same path as Croatia. And the new Croatian authority believed that the most important business they had to do was to change the constitutional position of Serbs. Karadzic supported the Krajina Serbs in their efforts to ensure their safe future and quoted them as an example if Bosnia were to take the path as Croatia did. That is the proper and genuine indictment that should have been signed by the OTP, but they are accusing me because I was in this position of high responsibility. Now, that was paragraphs 15 and 16. You see what Croatia looks like according to the new constitution. The Republic of Croatia establishes itself as the national state of the Croatian people and the state of the members of autonomous national minorities, the Serbs, Czechs, Slovaks, Italians, Hungarians, et cetera. And the Serbs joined Croatia together with the Krajina that belonged to them, which they got from Austro-Hungary, not from Croatia. Minister Boljkovac, whom you heard at the very beginning of the crisis in January 1991, now takes a position that is one of moral high ground and a repenting person. He says Croatia attacked the Serbs and Yugoslavia, not the other way round, and in order for you to see what that looked like, Saso Gersovski, a Macedonian, a conscript who was doing his army service in Split in May 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "[Previous translation continues] ... attacks, their families are being exposed to all sorts of pressures to compel them to move out of Slovenia and Croatia. You remember the first attacks on army members was the assault of the infuriated civilians, nationalists, on the soldiers who did their military service in Split. On that occasion soldier Sasa Gersovski was killed. Here are only some of the atrocities committed on officers in Zadar by the Ustasha Black Legions."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bjelovar, Split, an army in its own country, and this is how they lose their lives. These are somebody's children. Sasa Gersovski has parents. He has a family in Macedonia. And now let us have a look at what Warren Zimmermann says, who was not pro-Serb at all. Let us see what he says in this situation. The JNA was in its own country, a legitimate force. And the Prosecutor is charging me with supporting response to mobilisation and the departure of recruits who went into the only legitimate army, and he finds a connection between the Serb Democratic Party and the army. I shall tell you, Excellencies, since the SDS was a non-Communist Party and they, the army, viewed us the same way as they viewed the SDA and the HDZ. It's only when they realised that they could not spend a single night into -- in areas that were under HDZ and SDA control, that they realized that we were something different. The OTP is going to say that they were doing something -- something for the Serbs. No, these were Communist generals who did not like us but they realised that they didn't even dare spend the night in areas that were under HDZ and SDA control; only then did they realise they had to move their weapons to Serb areas; it was not for the Serbs’ sake. And for an entire year Croats and Muslims did not go into the army. They withdrew their own officers as well and created their own armies. The OTP is going to tell you that the JNA turned into the Army of Republika Srpska. All the armies in all parts of the former Yugoslavia came into existence on the basis of the JNA, except that the others were created later because they created their own armed formations over a long period of time; whereas the Serbs refused to create their own armed formations until the order was given for the Army of Yugoslavia, the army of their homeland, to withdraw from Bosnia. Of course these people, these individuals joined their own people, their own nation then. Now, let us see how Germany in 1991, just like in 1941, congratulated Croatia, its ally. I have to say to our Western allies from the First and Second World Wars that perhaps we should envy the Croats for their allies. Germany proved to be a far more reliable ally than our allies from the First and Second World Wars, who turned against the Serbs and who caused us great pain. That shows that the German victory in 1991 was full and definite. Now, let us see what the OTP is charging me with. They say that -- that our basic sin was the fact that we wanted to have a policy of our own, a continuity of the SDS and state structures. So the establishment of a political party among the Serbs is a crime. May I remind you that the Serbs were the last to set up a political party on ethnic grounds in Bosnia-Herzegovina, four months before the elections. All others formed their own parties before that, and they showed what their political programmes were of these political parties, and this caused great concern among the Serbs who then wanted to establish a political party of their own. Everything that the Serbs did, establish a party, establish an Assembly, take part in the elections, they did all of that, according to the OTP, in order to create a state of their own in Bosnia-Herzegovina and to expel from that state Muslims and Croats. Instead of isolating a particular crime that was committed by this accused person, instead of the OTP doing something like that, they are accusing Serbs for any activity they engaged in. They claim that that is joint criminal enterprise. They behaved not the way they wanted to. Serbs were not engaged in action. They were engaged in reaction. The Prosecution omits to say that, and they do not say what would have happened had there have been no action. Would the Serb reaction be the same? Who can say: We heard here at the last status conference that the Army of Republika Srpska legitimately reacted to Srebrenica and Zepa. How could crimes be committed had this action not be legitimate, had there not been for provocations? The Serb Democratic Party, it is stated here, was created in order to do something that never crossed their minds. No one thought that that kind of thing could happen. On the basis of the efforts made by the OTP, excellent people were convicted here, people I know well. Mr. Krajisnik, 20 years in prison, as if he led a gang of criminals. He was sentenced according to mafia laws and he headed a democratic Assembly. Wonderful men. Certain generals were indicted and convicted as if they were attacking an innocent population, not an army that was three times stronger than their own and that was committing such bestial acts. Here you are. You know the name of this young man whose head is being held here. That is what happened in Bosnia. That is the army that my generals fought against in their very own territory, just defending these territories against combatants of this kind, who were prepared to do this kind of thing and have their picture taken at that. But the OTP behaves as if the Serbs were doing something different. They were dealing with a raging bull, but the OTP claim that they were dealing with lambs and causing lambs irreparable harm. The basic problem of the OTP was the existence of the Serb Democratic Party. They say it was a centralist party. They say that the leader was a very fierce one, an autocrat, and so on and so forth. First of all, without an army and police you cannot do much among the Serbs and you cannot be an autocrat least of all. Serbs like to protest. It is hard to keep Serbs under control. And let us see what this leader advocated. The need of the OTP to present me as a monster is due to the fact that they don't have any evidence, and it's going to be easier for them to prove their case if they portray the accused as a monster rather than if they portray him as a real live person. It is very important that the OTP admitted that I personally did not commit any crimes. However, I think that that is very risky from the point of view of the Prosecution interests. If I did not commit a single crime, if it was, rather, committed by those who shared the same values with me, then the question has to be raised as to why they did that. According to the position of the OTP, they did that in order to attain certain objectives. However, it is totally absurd and paradoxical to have behaviour that is in total contravention of these interests ascribed to the Serbs. None of the Serbs' objectives can be attained in those ways, not even those criminal ones that the OTP ascribes to the Serbs. Ethnic cleansing. The Serb Democratic Party and Radovan Karadzic and the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina did their utmost, everything that could have been done, in order to avoid a war. Excellencies, now we're going to put things in their right place. We are going to look at the chronology of what happened, what was cause and what was effect, and what stemmed from all of this. Then we are going to see that this kind of chronological analysis is going to prove causality, sequence of events, the options at one's disposal. Let's see whether the Serbs could have done anything else. Then genuine, not false consequence. Just five seconds, Your Excellency, please. Then we're going to see that this indictment should not have been issued in the first place, because it is the crisis itself, the war itself that show what the reasons were, and there is no Serb responsibility for this. However, all of this is vague due to the position taken by the Prosecution, and this Prosecutor managed to -- or, rather, the Office of the Prosecutor managed to convince some Judges that things stand the way they portray them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will break for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. We visited Croatia for a while because it was the OTP who introduced Croatia. I have nothing against that, because it involves one people and one single crisis. Let me just remind you a little how this whole picture was created, starting from the beginning. In 1990, the League of Communists started to disintegrate because they failed to conclude their 14th convention. They disintegrated into ethnic and nationalist Leagues of Communists of various republics. At that point, Karadzic had been a dissident since 1968. I was living with my family. I had my friends and I was working, and I didn't believe that the Communists will ever leave power. However, that is what happened, and a multi-party system was created. On the 27th of March, 1990, a group of young Muslims known for having served lengthy prison sentences in various trials announced that they were going to form a Muslim party with Muslim objectives. This didn't concern the Serbs because in their programme they said they will not talk even to the parties who were not favouring Yugoslavia. However, very soon thereafter, graffiti targeting Serbs were seen on the old Serbian church. Already something to worry about. A Muslim party was created and their enemies were going to be the JNA and the Serbs. On the 15th of May, 1990, the forum for the protection of individual and traditional rights of Muslims was established. The Croatian elections took place on the 22nd of April. The HDZ, which was the most ethnic-based and the most extremist political party, had very successfully assimilated the Ustasha policies and they won the elections. So all of this was happening during that period. And then on the 26th of May, the Party of Democratic Action had its founding Assembly. It had been announced on the 27th of March. The Serbs, at that period, do not even have any plans for setting up their own party. We saw that this founding Assembly, Dalibor Brozovic said that Croatia was going to be defended on the River Drina although nobody had had attacked it, and that was only a month after the elections in Croatia. It was only on the 28th of June that the Serbs in Sarajevo and Bosnia, a strong community, renewed the operation of the cultural society called Prosvjeta, that the been banned both during World War II and immediately after World War II, and unfortunately I have to say that when it came to the Serbian questions, the Communists very often were acting in unison with the Ustasha and the German Nazis. They shared opinions on that issue. The Serbian Democratic Party was formed on the 12th of July by the Serbian intellectual and political elite under the pressure of the people, because they didn't know who to vote for. The HDZ already spilled over into the -- into Bosnia. They were seeing the banners of the HDZ and SDA being tied together in rallies, whereas the Serbs had nothing. Therefore, the Serbian intelligentsia was asked to establish the Serbian Democratic Party. Izetbegovic came to the rally, greeted us, and he said that he had expected this to happen sooner. Somebody from the audience asked him what were his views about Yugoslavia, and he said, "I'm in favour of a reasonable federation," and by that, Izetbegovic lay down the foundations for our coalition, possible coalition, by convincing us that there were no major differences between our political platforms. The Prosecution omitted, although they were searching for the elements of mens rea and the characters of those involved, the main players of the Serbian Democratic Party, but they omitted to say who founded the Serbian Democratic Party, whether those were extremists, losers, scum, or were they university professors, authors of many books, scientists, et cetera, who subsequently, by living for four years on the mountains and in deserted lands, became a party that had so many intellectuals amongst its ranks like no other party in Europe. They could boast very high level of expertise and knowledge, and they led a very small community in very hard times. This does not suit the Prosecution, and that is why they disregarded this. In their search for mens rea, Mr. Tieger went back into the past as far as Czar Dusan. He claims that I wanted to have what Czar Dusan had, and that was the ethnic-clean state. The Serbian state during his reign, in the 14th century, was a multi-ethnic state incorporating Serbs, Albanians, and other ethnic communities. Even today Serbia has probably the largest number of various ethnic communities. They haven't been assimilated, and their identity is being protected and preserved. Therefore, you cannot take Czar Dusan as an example for an ethnically clean state. We all know, as all the governments had proclaimed it even before Tito’s death, that if Yugoslavia falls apart, Bosnia would suffer the most; so I wrote a letter to Milan Kucan, proposing to everyone that we carry out a Scandinavisation. The countries of Scandinavia, in 1905, agreed to part peacefully. They had six months to decide in which country they wanted to live, and even today all these countries live happily, in prosperity next to one another. This accused was against the split-up of Bosnia-Herzegovina. However, when the secession started, he was in favour of turning Bosnia into a country made according to the model of Switzerland. It would be divided into cantons, and wherever there are thirty thousand of one group, fifty thousand of another or a third group, let them make a canton of their own. Cantons do not necessarily have to have territorial continuity, because at that time there was no war. It was only important for everyone to do their job and administer the country without any internal clashes and permanent attempts to dominate. I have to say that the issue of cantonisation was for the first time mentioned in a newspaper in Zagreb, but we accepted it immediately as a very good solution for saving Bosnia. While searching for mens rea and the intentions of the Serbian Democratic Party and when the OTP wants to prove that the SDS was, in fact, formed in order to start the war and form a Serbian state and expel others in the process, they do not invoke anything else other than things that happened only according to the logic of a civil war, not because the Serbian Democratic Party intended them to happen. Just like other nationalist parties, the SDS won around 98 per cent of votes. This implied a huge responsibility. We won that on a democratic programme, and the Prosecution was unable to show a single element of our responsibility that would have been instrumental in creating the events that followed. They couldn't find a single such thing, a single such cause in our documents. The OTP should not look what a deputy said if angered or something like that. They should just focus on the party platform and programme. We divided power in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and we created a coalition that was possible at the time. The Serbian Democratic Party, on behalf of the Serbian people that it represented, accept the post of the speaker. This is not in the executive branch. The Muslims had the president of the Presidency, and the Croats had the prime minister. Although they only constituted 17 per cent, but that didn't matter. No matter the percentage, they are on an equal footing, a constituent people. We didn't seek neither the Ministry of the Interior nor the Ministry of Defence. The Serbs wanted to be allocated the Ministry of Agriculture, because if you look at the map, these blue areas are the areas where the Serbs constitute majority nowadays, after all the various genocides, and that was the case before the war as well. That is why we were looking for the Ministry of Agriculture. I would like to remind the Chamber and the Prosecution of the fact that one cannot say that these people who have been a constituent people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that you cannot circumvent them when to making serious decisions. Just because somebody is set on violating the Constitution and the laws and, based on mere numerical prevalence, even without any requirements met for making such a decision democratically - these people have to swallow that and that to accept the dictate of the other two parties. That was not an option for us. We got the Ministry of Science and the Ministry of Information. In short, there was not a single ministry in our hands that would serve war efforts. Immediately after the elections, this accused, due to tensions, made a proposal for creating an expert government. Those were people who had been dissidents for a long time and they were not popular among the Communists. For that we proposed that the party people should not be in the government but, rather, people who are professionals. This Accused also did not run for any positions, because he had recommended to his party colleagues that party cadres not be taken on into the government, that technocrats be chosen instead. The other two parties didn't accept that, but the SDS stood by its position. There was only one Serb minister who was a member of the Serbian Democratic Party, and that was the Minister of Information. Of the others, in the Communist times, two had held ministerial positions. We took the Ministry of Justice, we took what I said, finance, agriculture, etc. So how is it possible for the Prosecution to overlook these efforts on the part of the Serbian Democratic Party, and how can the intentions to wage war, that go back to the 12th of July, how can they reconcile that with the fact that they had the ministries in their hands that I mentioned they had and that they were willing to give power to professionals? This is probably a trap that the Prosecution fell into due to their lack of knowledge of the language. On the eve of the war and the most serious crisis, when we got the right to have our constituent unit, to have the police, the National Guard and the government, the words of this accused were: "This is what we agreed. Go out into the field. Take power into your hands and act responsibly." This is being translated by the OTP "Take over." And one of the main things in this indictment is the claim that the Serbs took over power in municipalities. But, Excellencies, if you look at this map, there was no need for Serbs to take over power but just to administer power that they won in the elections. Why would they take it over? From whom? They were already in power there, and you can see that from this map. Why would we take over power from someone in Bijeljina? And Bijeljina features here as a municipality that was taken over by force. But this lack of knowledge of language, when somebody takes over a tool, it means he is taking a tool that belongs to someone else. And when somebody takes up a tool, it means he is picking up his own tool that was lying there, and he just picks it up. So this is a drastic difference between these two terms, and this gave rise to this Indictment. Not only didn't we take the Ministry of the Interior, but we didn't even have our own people at any of the lower levels in that ministry. All the people who were there had already been in the police. We didn't bring any criminals. I would draw your attention to the intercept of the conversation between the accused and the deputy minister, which is a confirmation that this deputy minister was not a member of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] I want to ask them if it's in the interest of the Muslim people to appoint only criminals at the MUP. "Karadzic: Vito, we haven't appointed a single criminal. "Zepinic: Yes, but I'm talking about that. "Karadzic: Look, please. We have nothing to be ashamed of. We have not brought a single man who hasn't been at the MUP. Their interest was, Vito, to bring on board loyal men. Listen to me carefully. They brought on board loyal men. And they did put one over on us, they double-crossed us while we were taking on professionals, honest people who had nothing to do with the party. "Zepinic: I'm going to send an open letter to the SDA and expressly ask them whether it's in the interests of the Muslim people to appoint only criminals. "Karadzic: We asked who was the most honest and the most competent and we appointed them, and mind you, now we in a dead-end street. They were appointing the most loyal people. We were appointing the most competent people."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that was this -- this difference in approach of the SDA and the Serb community and this core of the fundamentalist SDA party. The difference in moral approach. And this led to the fact that the police in Bosnia-Herzegovina started to massively abuse their state authority against the Serb people and for the SDA. The gentleman talking to me was appointed as deputy minister in the Serb place. He wasn't a member of the SDS. We didn't do things like that. But they changed the entire picture of the police force. They brought in criminals and they started to arm the people and to arm the Party of Democratic Action and the Patriotic League as well, which was formed very early on, the 31st of March, two months after the joint government had been set up. So this is proof and evidence that we get from this intercept, that the number two man in the MUP confirms that yes, they were bringing in criminals, we were not, and that we still maintain that professionals should be used, honest professionals, and not party people in the distribution of power and authority and political posts. Now, it would be very useful if we were to see and look at what Mr. Izetbegovic says under these circumstances, faced with this situation. On the 27th of February to the 15th of January, he was in favour of Yugoslavia. However, on the 27th of February of that same year, just one month after the coalition government was formed, Izetbegovic says that he will give up peace for Bosnia's independence and sovereignty but he would not be ready to sacrifice sovereign Bosnia for peace. So it is his resolve to go to the very end regardless of whether he has the right to do so, whether he is right or not, and whether the people living on two-thirds of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina -- well, there's one-third of the population there who were Serbs, because genocide reduced that group of the population. So, the Prosecution is suggesting that Serbs should have accepted that Muslims and Croats were exploiting the results of the genocide against the Serbs. They want to reap their own benefit because now they're saying there's no more than a third of you, but we can see where they were the majority when they were in the majority. They were the majority on two-thirds -- in two-thirds of Bosnia, two-thirds of Bosnian territory, and they were reduced because of the genocide during World War II. Otherwise, they were always the majority population before. Now, who are these people with whom we entered into a coalition government and who conditioned our behaviour fully? We're going to see that. Let's see what the leading ideology was of this group of people. Since the Prosecution is seeking mens rea for all of us, let's see who we were dealing with. Were they docile lambs or were we up against something to which we had to react and react in the way we did? Mr. Izetbegovic, in 1970, for example, published -- or, rather, wrote and distributed secretly, clandestinely, the Islamic Declaration. Mr. Izetbegovic in 1941, 2, and 3, was a member of the young Muslims organisation, and at the time, he opted for the introduction of a fundamentalist Islamic regime everywhere on territory inhabited by the Muslims, and the bases and foundations of that programme was the Islamic Declaration which he wrote in 1970. Now after the war, after World War II, he continued to propagate clandestinely and subversively and he was sentenced to three years' imprisonment after World War II. After he left prison, he was one of the individuals that you should take your hat off to, actually, because of his perseverance and because he didn't want to give way. He wanted to stick to his programme, and he never changed on that score. During World War II, he and his collaborators, the Behmen brothers, received this man who is on that picture there with Hitler. He is the Grand Mufti of Jerusalem, El Husseini, who was in Sarajevo several times, at least twice in fact, and he went to see Hitler umpteen times. And every time he came to Bosnia, this resulted in the establishment of the Waffen SS Division which was called the Handzar Sword Division, which was the most brutal division. You couldn't even imagine how brutal they were and the brutalities they committed. It was the most brutal unit ever. So that was Hitler's friend as you can see and a guest with Behmen and Izetbegovic. Therefore, after the war, Mr. Izetbegovic, as I said, was in prison. He was given a prison sentence, and in 1970 he wrote the Islamic Declaration which is, in fact, the programme of the Party of Democratic Action. Of course, we hoped that it wasn't what it was, but it proved to be exactly what we -- what it was and I saw sought ways and means, in 1990, to save Bosnia, and I wanted Izetbegovic to give up on the Islamic Declaration and tell us that it wasn't the political programme of the SDA. We know he never gave us those assurances. He remained firm. Not only has the Prosecution not sought to find who our partners were that conditioned our behaviour, but erroneously interprets our words and says, when I'm speaking at a meeting, I think it was an Assembly session or a party meeting, said that: "We cannot control the Muslims in such a unitary state. We know very well when fundamentalism turns up that we cannot live together. There is no tolerance anymore." Now, what is this all about? What has the Prosecution done here? It cut off part of my speech and made this sentence stand alone and failed to print the main sentence, and this is something that is often done. But actually what it was was that the West, and it proved to be true, did not allow Republika Srpska to be established or the Serbs to remain in Yugoslavia, perhaps because it did not want to enable the Muslims to be an express -- a majority and to form an Islamic state in Europe. The thesis is that the Serbs and Croats should remain in Bosnia to control the Islamic factor to the advantage of Europe, as a tool for Europe, and Radovan Karadzic says that's not a good thing. The Serbs will not -- Karadzic won't allow the Serbs to be used as a controlling factor of the Islamic group, and also it would be much more peace loving if the Serbs would get away from this fundamentalist project rather than having them oppose it. Why should the Serbs once again stand at the gates of the -- stand at Europe's gates and preserve Europe and protect it as in the famous book about the Serbs as the gatekeepers of Europe? So here what the Prosecution is trying to do is to say that we, in fact, wished to control the Muslims, whereas we're stating quite the reverse. We say we don't want to do that. We don't want to lay down our lives for that. Similarly, another Assembly deputy says that we were set to be the executioners of the Muslims in Bosnia, and we said we don't want to do that, but what the Prosecution says is that is precisely what we chose to do, to be the executioners. And then he went on to say, an institution 700 years old, probably thinking about the Vatican, has set us the role of being executioners, whereas we refuse to be executioners. And this is being reversed by the Prosecutor. So, were it not for such forgeries, there wouldn't have been an indictment. You have to read what the man actually said. It's not that we chose to be executioners; they thought that we could perform the function of executioners, but we refused to play that role. Furthermore the Prosecution, in paragraph 23 of their pre-trial brief, states that, without foundation, I told our people that we faced the same plans, the same villains, and the same victims as in World War II, and that I insisted that the Muslims sought an Islamic state and were preparing laws to subjugate Serbs, and that Serbs were unwilling to go back to slavery. And what if that's true, and that is something the Prosecution should have established. The Prosecution's position is that this wasn't true, but we will prove that it is true. Why waste time and money by holding trials of this kind? Had an investigating magistrate been in charge of this, he would have concluded Karadzic was right, the Prosecution was wrong, because there's too much evidence and proof to show that that is so. But let's see whether it is true and what the situation is. Mr. Izetbegovic was the creator of an organisation which has been existence for 50 years, that is since 1939 onwards, which had an oath of this kind. It says: "Glory and praise to Allah, the Lord of all worlds, as a member of the organization"... This first part is normal. "As a member of the organization, I swear to Almighty Allah, among other things, that I will sacrifice everything on God's path including my life, if the interests of Islam require that. I will fight uncompromisingly against everything non-Islamic. I will sacrifice everything on God's path including my life, if the interests of Islam require that. I will also fight for the grandeur and fame of Islam. So may God give me the power to do that on the road of jihad." Yes. I'm being told to slow down so I have to do so. So this is the oath, the oath taken by the Muslim youth. Now let's look and see what Mr. Izetbegovic says in his Islamic Declaration. What are Islam's tasks or the tasks of Muslims? The Muslims must be a movement, and that movement can take over power and authority as soon as it is morally and otherwise strong enough to topple not only the current non-Islamic government, but to build up an Islamic government. So they don't have do wait 50 per cent because waiting 50 per cent means waiting for a democracy of some kind, with some kind of voting. But as soon as -- what he's saying is as soon as they feel strong enough, they are duty-bound to topple everything non-Islamic. After he came out of prison for the first time, Mr. Izetbegovic wrote this Islamic Declaration and became a member of some important institutions. That's something that the Prosecution doesn't know about but the political committee in the US Senate does, the US Senate Republican Policy Committee, the whole world knows about that. However, the Prosecutor is trying to make me out to be a barbarian attacking a good neighbour, a good and peaceful neighbour. This is what the US Senate Republican Policy Committee says, what it said in 1998, about what Mr. Izetbegovic said in 1983. Here is what a Republican Senate, a Republican-dominated Senate, said about this in 1998: that in 1983, Mr. Izetbegovic stepped up his efforts, begun in 1979, to introduce Islamic rule in Bosnia-Herzegovina. At his 1983 trial – that was his second trial, where 65 witnesses were heard before the Grand Chamber made up of 5 judges – all five judges were Muslims, and 62 of the witnesses were Muslims. Now, the judgement for Alija Izetbegovic, Omer Behmen, Hasan Cengic, they were all alive and active in 1990, the judgement and sentence says that they were taken over by the idea of Islamisation and the Islamic revival, and that this began in 1974, that is to say, the year of the promotion of the new Yugoslav constitution which laid the foundations for the break-up of Yugoslavia in the first place, and that they had accepted the Islamic revolution as being their own Iranian revolution. He says -- he refers to this as the Islamic population, that conditions should be created for Bosnia to become an Islamic republic with Islamic laws, and that would refer to everybody living in Bosnia, and he says the imams in Bosnia should be armed just like the Iranian Shiite imams in Iran. Now, in that same year, that is to say already in 1982, Izetbegovic identifies the Serbs as the enemies. There's no Karadzic. There's no Milosevic on the scene. There's no memorandum by the Serbian Academy of Arts and Sciences, none of that. And all the apparatuses that the Prosecution is aiming against the Serbs and takes to be -- to prove that the Serbs are the culprits. Kosovo and Vojvodina were provinces of Serbia. It was the only republic that was not able to resolve its problems, and thanks to a Macedonian, Lazar Kolisevski, we uncovered what was afoot. It was a -- the Communist slogan was, A weak Serbia will make a strong Yugoslavia. The weaker Serbia, the stronger Yugoslavia. Well, that weak Serbia in 1982, according to Izetbegovic, was the enemy. It was the foe. His associate Omer Behmen, with whom he co-operated during World War II as well and in whose house the mufti stayed when he visited, the Husseini muftis of Jerusalem, he said that there was pressure being exerted on Muslims. And the other man or the third man, Cengic, says that a Muslim could not feed a Serb child, nurse a Serb child. Mr. Cengic at the time, because Karadzic isn't there yet, we're dealing with 1984 and 1983, no SDS, so he says what the goal of their revolution is, the revolution that they were preparing. So if you envisage the map of Yugoslavia, Bosnia, Sandzak, Kosovo, we call it the green transversal over there, you know. Now, the Prosecutor doesn't agree with that. He considers that we shouldn't even -- it should never enter our heads. Now, the minister of Turkey comes and says that he's going to reinstate that green transversal. And in 1990, Turgut Ozal said that Turkey would stretch from the Adriatic to the Great Wall of China. Well, yes, maybe, but without the Serbs because we're not going to take part in that kind of empire. So here we have the green transversal plotted by a mighty man, who is a clergyman as well, yes, a clergyman, and the American clergyman who was publicly was sorry that Cengic wasn't killed on time seems to be a lamb compared to this one, and he says you don't need a pretext for that, and then in another place he says you should make a pretext. So we saw Markale, for example, and the other pretexts that were created and fabricated, and then based on that, they behaved towards the Serbs as if it was the Serbs to blame. Now, I wasn't surprised to see them doing it, but why is the Prosecution following suit and why is it asking this Tribunal and the Trial Chamber to do the same, to accept war trickery and cunning? There was a second incidence of Markale later on. They were technically better prepared but the same technology was used and for the same reasons. And this is an image of Izetbegovic's trial in 1983, and the second man is Behmen. I don't remember who the others were but it's the Izetbegovic et al trial. Now, we see that the plans are the same, the victims are the same, and the perpetrators are the same, just as they were in World War II. The Prosecutor -- the Prosecutor, however, considers otherwise, and this is what the judgement states, the judgement in 1983, the Chamber of five, all Muslims, 62 Muslim witnesses, says: "In all circumstances, advocating such an ideology would mean returning to the state of civil war. It is indisputable that such an ideology cannot be implemented in a community which is religiously and politically so profoundly mixed" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: A little slower, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on the screen, that's why I'm hurrying. A community which is religiously and politically so profoundly mixed that the dominance or complete supremacy of any of the existing national entities is simply inconceivable, unless based on terror or possibly foreign intervention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, slow down further, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, let's look at this and I'd like the Prosecution to look at it, too. Take a look at this. Now seven years after this, after this judgement, we see the realisation and implementation of that very ideology, but not with terror or foreign intervention but both terror and foreign intervention. And the Trial Chamber and the Judges here were very far-sighted because it was terror and calls for foreign intervention. Markale were calls for foreign intervention. It was montage and fabrication, the butchery of one’s own people, and you will see that in the programme they had that too, the butchery of one's own people. That is written down. You'll come to see that when we look at the programme. And now the Prosecutor, in addition to everything that is at -- is at its disposal, says that Karadzic insisted on as much separation as possible. Well, if our neighbours are preparing a programme of this kind and life of this kind, of course we're going to separate from them. We don't believe that that's what the Muslim masses wanted. So it wasn't Izetbegovic but Abdic who won the elections. The Muslims cried out to the Muslims and Serbs. They applauded them when there was this historical agreement in the offing, in 1991, until Izetbegovic withdraw it. They were all very happy and applauded because the Serbs and Muslims managed to reach an agreement. However, that group chose to manipulate the SDA and the entire Muslim community. Now let us have a look at what things would be like if we were to write a genuine indictment and if we were to just to change the names. Izetbegovic insisted on the secession of all Bosnia despite Bosnia's ethnically intermingled character. This meant making Serbs a national minority in his Islamic republic and taking them out of the country. That is to say, that if Muslims and Serbs are intermingled in Republika Srpska, then Republika Srpska cannot be established; but if the Serbs are intermingled with the Muslims in all of Bosnia, then it can happen. It seems that Muslims are more intermingled than Serbs and all in the same place. However, they somehow manage to intermingle more. You will see how figures are dealt with in very relative terms. As the learned Mr. Tieger says, who likes cursory glances, he says, Let's cast a cursory glance at this map. What about the Serbs in Bosnia? I mean, when I say the Serbs own land, they own land in terms of private ownership, but Serbs are a majority population in this area, and they have the right to say, once they had attained the right to statehood and lived in Yugoslavia, they had the right to say whether they are willing to accept interventions of this kind, foreign interventions, ideologies that hurt both Muslims and Serbs a great deal. Does the Prosecution approve, say, the Prosecution says 30 per cent. Now, do they approve -- or actually, have a look at it. This is what it would look like. We insisted upon separating from them, but let's look at it this way: Izetbegovic insisted on secession of all of Bosnia despite Bosnia's ethnically intermingled character. It would mean that he can take a million and a half Serbs out, and the Prosecution says that we sought the territories of Republika Srpska where there were hundreds of thousands of Muslims and Croats. They seem to be more than a million and a half Serbs for the Prosecution. That's something that we don't understand. Except that these Muslims and Croats who would stay in Republika Srpska, they wouldn't leave their own state; they would just live in a different entity but within their own country. Again this was abused. We cannot control the Muslims, et cetera, et cetera. That sentence has been brutalised, butchered, and, when it is shown to the Judges, of course they will confirm the indictment, it is not for the Judges to carry out investigations, but all of this was abused. They just took parts of this sentence, cut it up. There are three sources, three major sources of artificial population growth rates, and that is not only the birth rate. First of all, the promoted migration of Muslims from Sandzak. Secondly, plans to resettle the alleged descendants of the Muslim emigrants to Turkey, and thirdly the fatwa that a Muslim woman should have five children so that one could be sacrificed for Bosnia. Why must she bear 5 children? So that they can outnumber the Serbs? We are against that kind of birth rate, yes. And when the Prosecution says that I said that we would not allow them to make settlements in Republika Srpska, I am saying to them what I'm saying to Mr. Izetbegovic. I said, Mr. Izetbegovic, I know what your plan is, that you want to bring in Muslims from Sandzak and Turks from Turkey. However, don't fool yourselves that we are going to allow you to make these settlements in Serb areas. Protestants or Catholics in Northern Ireland would not allow that either. To have a conscious effort made by way of political action in order to disrupt the ethnical balance, that is a crime. We are not going to allow that to happen. That's what I said before our Assembly or wherever, at some meeting. So I was just interpreting what I had said to Izetbegovic. I had said that to them, and he was just blinking and he said, "I understand." Now, let us see what this Islamic Declaration is. This is a programme text. Regardless of whether the Communists were in power or not, nothing has changed whatsoever. It says: "We announce, to our friends and foes alike, that Muslims are determined to take the fate of the Islamic world into their own hands, and we are going to set up a world in accordance with our own precepts. The struggle already knows of its shahids. These are the holy warriors that die in such wars, martyrs. They're martyrs, actually. A shahid is a martyr. A Muslim can die only with the name of Allah on his lips and for the glory of Islam, or escape from the battle-field." Let me stop at this point for a moment and say that we're going to bring proof of this, Mr. Izetbegovic saying to his associates, For tactical reasons we say that our soldiers are laying their lives for a multi-ethnic Bosnia, but let us not fool ourselves, they are not dying for a multi-ethnic Bosnia. That was a moment of frankness, sincerity, in a narrow circle, but we have that evidence. The first most important conclusion is that the Islamic religion and non-Islamic social and political institutions cannot co-exist. There can be neither peace nor co-existence between the Islamic religion and non-Islamic social and political institutions. Whoever wishes our community well will not spare a struggle, danger and misfortune. The Islamic movement should and can start to take over power as soon as it is morally and numerically strong enough to be able to do that in their own territory. So this is not a lay state. The state should support the moral precepts of religion. Islam is the first point and pan-Islamism is the second point. Now, please have a look at this. As we announce renewal, we are not announcing a period of safety and peace but of unrest and challenges. There are many things that are to be destroyed. People who are asleep can only be awakened by blows. Who wishes our community well should not spare it of exertions, dangers, and troubles. Islamic renewal can start without a political revolution, but it cannot be brought to a successful end without a political revolution. The movement has to take power as soon as it is strong enough, numerically strong enough to be able to overturn not only the existing non-Islamic government but also to build up a new Islamic one. That is what is unequivocally stated, no dilemma whatsoever. Unrest, challenges. It just looks like blood, sweat and tears, as Churchill had put it, because it is the enemy that causes blood, sweat, and tears among Churchill's people. Whereas here it is one's own government that is going to cause blood, sweat and tears among their own people. Who wishes our community well should not spare them, should hit them and in this waking them up. The blow, the hit was Markale. So that the people could stand strong against the Serbs, they will try to prove that it is the Serbs who did that at Markale, and you saw how unconvincing that is. It is impossible to do that with a single shell, especially kill that many people who are not there in the first place. That is what happened in 1990, and that is the moment when the renewal is being heralded and when there is going to be a period of unrest and challenges because many things are seeking their own destroyers. We did not ask for any destroyers. These that will be destroyed and that were begging for destruction were the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, secular government. There will be no compromise with secular states here. Then the JNA, the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, life and co-existence in Bosnia-Herzegovina, common roots. The Muslim speaks the same language we do, the Serbian language. The fact that you accepted such a thing as the Bosnian language is a manipulation, that is wrong because the Serbian language is heritage of the Serb people. Australians do not speak the Australian language or an Australian language, they speak English. Then common past was destroyed but also the common present and the common future. We didn't ask for that. They asked for that, or they thought that they had the right to do that, although no one did call upon them to do it. Now, let us see what accusations levelled at the Serbs are like. They have to cut up sentences and mutilate them; whereas here they have prepared documents. They were held accountable before courts of law because of these texts that were written, and they didn't want to give up on them. They rather went to prison. The Serb Democratic Party, even before 1990, asked for a chamber of nations to be introduced in the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and such a Chamber would decide on important matters by way of consensus. That proposal does not correspond to a joint criminal enterprise. If that were the case, what could the Serbs do against the Muslims and the Croats? Nothing. Everybody would have the right to veto. They responded by establishing this council for the equal rights of peoples and nationalities. This is clumsy Communist language and jargon. It is very long and clumsy. So they would meet ad hoc. It's not a regular body. If we run into some kind of trouble then it would meet. I mean, had that been applied, then that would be some kind of guarantee that we would not be brought into this position but the Serb -- it's not only the Serbs but also the Muslims and the Croats who would not be brought into a difficult position to accept something that was unacceptable. In every particular case, the Serbs, the Serb Democratic Party and this accused person proposed solutions that are directly contrary to what they are being charged for. This is part of the constitution. There was this declaration on sovereignty that was stopped twice through this council, but it was never established because the SDA sabotaged its establishment. So it was practically as if it had never been set up. When I made that speech, on the 15th of October, they simply overrode that. They said, We're not interested. Because even in March, Mr. Izetbegovic said, in Split, when there was a conference of the presidents of the Yugoslav republics, he said, We are going to adopt that with or without the Serbs, that is to say, either with the Serbs or against the Serbs. Please, the OTP denies us the right to political life and reciprocal measures. They even claim that we simply had to remain silent, to bow to this illegally declared referendum and the unlawfully achieved sovereignty and independence that were envisaged and that destroyed our rights to such an extent. Also, the legal system which was a backbone, as it is in any society, and that stems from the Islamic Declaration as an act of destruction; whereas the Prosecution claims that we were not supposed to do anything about it. Everything that we did was a crime on our part. However, that is what was written. We had the right to challenge this. Mr. Izetbegovic says, We are completely aware that by declaring the neutrality of Bosnia-Herzegovina in relation to the war in Croatia, we may have violated certain laws, but at the moment everything is fluid. There are laws and there are laws. That is to say, there are laws that we're going to abide by if they suit us and there are laws, on the other hand, that we are not going to observe if they benefit others. Now, that is that fluid situation that Karadzic is going to speak of, where Serbs cannot find their way in these unlawful situations. The Prosecution is going to hold that against us as well. However, that was the basis for chaos in Bosnia-Herzegovina. This existence of laws and other laws. It can be done this way or that way. Let us see how Bosnia and Herzegovina could have functioned. They could not attain any kind of independence without Serb approval. They had to decide by a two-third majority. There was no two-third majority at the referendum, there would not have been a two-third majority in parliament either because 83 Serbs were against it, 83 Serb MPs, and they separated from the Bosnian parliament and they established the Assembly of the Serb people. So there was no way for Bosnia and Herzegovina to adopt this resolution on sovereignty unless they said there are laws and again there are laws on the other hand. So if we did not agree to act unlawfully, there is nothing that they could do. If someone were to say to us whether we, as Serbs, were denied our right to defence, was our right to reciprocity taken away from us, to a response to unlawful behaviour, to violations of our rights, to breaches of the constitution. If that was not the case, then this indictment is impossible, and it should have been rejected straight away. It should be rejected now as well if we prove that we never intended to throw Muslims and Croats out of their home. We did not consider Bosnia or Republika Srpska to be our home. We thought that Yugoslavia was our home. That was what we believed, and that is what we are going to prove very soon. The values of Bosnian society that were hoping to see its destroyers, we didn't want to be any part of that. The Serbs, the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina at that point in time had the explicit right, according to the constitution, but also historically viewed they had the right to be a constituent people that were forming this joint state and they were co-owners, as it were, of this Bosnia-Herzegovina, just like the Serbs of Krajina were the co-owners of Croatia because they had entered this joint venture. Now, a change of the status, the constitutional legal status of Bosnia-Herzegovina had to evolve in accordance with the law. Serbs were more than one-third. If you were to take into account Serbs, and about one-third or one-quarter of them were Serbs who were in favour of the creation of a Yugoslav nation, there were more than one-third of Serbs in the population and they are sufficient not only in terms of consensus but also through every other democratic process. They could have stopped independence. It is peoples, not administrative territories that had the right to independence and self-determination. You know how the Serbs got into Yugoslavia? In 1918, a country was established of Serb, Croats, and Slovenes from the newly liberated territories of Austro-Hungary. There was not different republics that were established. There was one single state that was established. So the Serbs were sovereign in Ljubljana, and Slovenes were in Sarajevo. Then that state asked the international community for permission to unite with Serbia. They united with Serbia. Serbs joined that state as co-owners of that state. That was what it was said that peoples had the right to self-determination. President Wilson said that Serbia should be given access to the sea, and the successors of President Wilson still owe this to Serbia. He has made this pledge. So we didn't have republics joining into Yugoslavia so that they can disjoin later. And as Lord Owen said, then they drew the administrative borders that suddenly became more important than the external borders. This was done totally arbitrarily. Nobody can say on what basis these administrative borders were drawn. Tito said it doesn't matter. Now suddenly they have become more important and blood was starting to be shed because of the borders, which is always the case when you have Communist borders or Imperial borders. If you look at Croatia, Croatia inherited Austro-Hungarian borders. The Serbs of Trebinje can see the seashore but cannot have access to it. This is what Hasan Cengic, a clergyman, says about the Patriotic League, formed on the 31st of March, 1991. I would like the Prosecution to show me a single formation behind which the Serbian Democratic Party or the Serbian people stood. However, what we have here, even before the 31st of March, a unit formed in Foca by the father of this Hasan Cengic, whilst the SDA was organising and leading its phalanxes from March until the beginning of the war. So this is the chart of the Patriotic League. The Commander-in-Chief is Alija Izetbegovic. The Main Staff is led by Sefer Halilovic, who was, I think, acquitted here. Then you had regional clergical [as interpreted] staff and regional military staffs, and at the bottom municipal political staffs and municipal military staffs. This organisation was very quickly manned and staffed so that in January 1994 they already had around 100.000 troops. So this is the role of the Patriotic League, of the Green Berets, and the other organisations that existed at the time. In these indictments against Serbs, the Prosecution is mainly focused on Crisis Staffs. The Serbs had their Crisis Staffs. When there's a shortage of gas, like it happened recently due to Ukrainian cutting off gas supplies, you have to establish a Crisis Staff. The situation is totally irregular, and you need a Crisis Staff to deal with it. But I would like to draw your attention first to the fact that the Crisis Staff of the Party of Democratic Action and the HDZ were present everywhere, even in the smallest village, much before the war and before of the inception of the SDS. Here are some of the differences between the Crisis Staffs of the SDA and the SDS. The SDA's Crisis Staff had been formed well before the war when there was no indication of the war breaking out in Bosnia-Herzegovina. SDS staffs were public and were only formed on the eve of the war, at the time when the SDA managed to bring the state structure to collapse. And the war in Croatia produced terrible problems and numerous refugees. The existence of the Patriotic League was already evident. We had armed formations, covert transportation of armaments and overt transportation of armaments, the existence of SDA crisis staffs, et cetera. It was only then that the Serbs established their Crisis Staff.
