The SDA crisis staffs were secret, conspiratorial, with powers and tasks that a secret executive power has, and the tasks that are entrusted to defence ministers and army general staffs. However, the SDS Crisis Staff's only function was to inform the Sarajevo headquarters as quickly as possible of all dangerous and clandestine goings-on. On the 14th of February, 1992, Karadzic tells them explicitly: "You are not an authority in power. You are there to help, to monitor the transportation of weapons, to monitor what's going on, and to let us know if there were any extraordinary situation." I quoted the example of the British people where Britain -- every Britain guards and protects his own country. The SDA Crisis Staffs took over the function of state authorities in municipalities. They were controlled by the republican Crisis Staff established at the Presidency, led by Ejup Ganic, who dubbed as the chief of the main political staff of the Patriotic League. It enabled Alija Izetbegovic to circumvent Biljana Plavsic and Nikola Koljevic as representatives of the Serbian people. They didn't have to adopt anything at the meeting. The Crisis Staff would make a decision that would normally have to be put to a vote and be debated, but in this way he bypassed them. The SDS Crisis Staff existed for a short period of time before the war, and once the war broke out they ceased to exist, and we had municipal Crisis Staff as state organs. So these staffs were neither the staffs of the SDS of the Serbs but, rather, the staffs of the authorities, and they were made up of the Muslims and Croats in the municipalities where these ethnicities lived. Here, for example, the Prosecution says that one report from the Bijeljina SDS Crisis Staff informs the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party of what the municipal Crisis Staff had decided. However, the Prosecution says it was decided by the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Democratic Party, whereas it is clearly written that the party’s Crisis Staff reports on what was decided by the authorities, and what by the municipal Crisis Staff as a state body. This only expedited the whole process, and there was no need for the Assembly to convene, and these decisions were later on adopted at regular assemblies. Crisis Staffs in Republika Srpska operated openly and publicly. They meticulously recorded every decision that they made, and they submitted them for adoption to their respective assemblies. For example, Kotor Varos had daily meetings of the Crisis Staffs, and this is an illustration of how responsible authority operates, like the one in Kotor Varos. But the OTP removed that example. However, I intend to bring it back just to show you how a responsible body of authority operates. Now, this is what they say about their achievements, that is to say, the heads of the SDA and the Patriotic League. Every local commune in municipality had several communes. In all 103 municipalities, the leadership of Patriotic League had their units ranging from a squad to a company. One of their tasks was to procure weapons. If you look back and remember the map that I showed you before, that means that in all these municipalities where the Serbs were living, there were a total of 109, because they -- they couldn't do this in the Croatian municipalities. However, in all these municipalities where Serbs lived they had their companies, and their Serbian neighbours were able to see that. And Prosecution thinks that we should be banned from observing and monitoring such activities. On the other hand, they allowed them to have these kind of units in their local communes. And they also criticise me for intimidating Serbs without any cause whatsoever. The entire preparations of -- were co-ordinated by the Patriotic League and its staffs throughout the territory of Bosnia or Islamic Bosnia, regardless of whether Serbs were living there or whether they were willing to accept what the Patriotic League and the SDA wanted. Mr. Izetbegovic met them. He gave his approval. He was their Commander-in-Chief. Now, look at this. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to adjourn very soon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have three more minutes, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, one minute.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: One minute. Okay. [Interpretation] Mr. Izetbegovic, by virtue of his position, was the chairman of the National Defence Council, Bosnia-Herzegovina. In February he forms a secret council for the defence of Muslims. So one Izetbegovic should arrest the other Izetbegovic, because these two occupied two different positions, and one of those positions was undermining the republic of the other one. And that is what the Serbs couldn't withstand any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, that's for today. Mr. Tieger, I'd like to make sure that we can hear you first thing tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we expect to be filing something today, and I can foreshadow that for the Court. I believe we'll be -- we won't be opposing certification. We will be opposing a stay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That would be helpful. 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 2nd day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.
